candidates.abstract: Join a major Western Sydney civil infrastructure project delivering earthworks, roads and utilities. Strong pipeline and genuine career growth.
candidates.content_text:
Project Engineer – Civil Infrastructure Western Sydney (near Western Sydney Airport) | Immediate Start
 Join a major civil infrastructure project helping deliver critical works within one of Australia's fastest-growing development corridors.
 ABOUT THE ROLE
 We are seeking an experienced Project Engineer to support the delivery of a large-scale civil infrastructure project involving bulk earthworks, utilities, roads, drainage and associated subdivision works.
 Working closely with the Project Manager and site delivery team, you will play a key role in coordinating subcontractors, managing consultant and design interfaces, resolving technical queries and ensuring works are delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with project requirements.
 The role will involve significant coordination between site teams, subcontractors, design consultants and external stakeholders to ensure design documentation, approvals and construction activities remain aligned with the project programme.
 This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing contractor with a strong pipeline of work across Western Sydney.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 - Coordinate day-to-day project delivery activities across multiple work fronts.
 - Manage subcontractors, suppliers, consultants and design interfaces.
 - Coordinate with civil, structural, services and other design consultants to resolve technical and construction-related issues.
 - Manage subcontractor RFIs, technical queries and design clarifications, ensuring timely responses from relevant consultants.
 - Support design management activities, including design reviews, documentation coordination, constructability assessments and design changes.
 - Monitor design deliverables, approvals and outstanding information to ensure construction activities remain on programme.
 - Prepare and manage RFIs, NCRs, ITPs, SWMS reviews and project documentation.
 - Monitor programme, productivity and project milestones.
 - Assist with procurement, scope packages and subcontractor management.
 - Track project costs, variations and progress claims.
 - Support quality assurance and compliance activities across site.
 - Liaise with client representatives, authorities and key project stakeholders.
 - Prepare regular project reporting and progress updates.
 - Drive efficient project outcomes through proactive problem solving and coordination.
 SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
 - Experience as a Project Engineer within civil infrastructure, subdivisions or earthworks projects.
 - Strong understanding of bulk earthworks, roads, drainage and utility installation.
 - Demonstrated experience coordinating engineering consultants and managing design-related issues during construction.
 - Ability to manage subcontractor RFIs, technical queries and design documentation.
 - Experience reviewing construction drawings, identifying design discrepancies and coordinating practical solutions.
 - Strong subcontractor management, project documentation and stakeholder coordination skills.
 - Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple work fronts in a live construction environment.
 - Strong communication, organisational and problem-solving skills.
 - Proficient with project management and reporting systems such as Procore, Laminar or similar.
 - Relevant Civil Engineering qualification.
 THE OPPORTUNITY
 - Major infrastructure project within the Western Sydney Airport growth corridor.
 - Long-term project pipeline and strong job security.
 - Exposure to large-scale civil infrastructure and subdivision works.
 - Broad involvement across engineering, design coordination and construction delivery.
 - High-performing and collaborative project team.
 - Genuine career progression opportunities.
 THE DETAILS
 - Full-time, site-based position.
 - Western Sydney location.
 - Competitive salary package based on experience.
 - Immediate start available.
 HOW TO APPLY
 Apply now or contact us for a confidential discussion about the opportunity.
candidates.teaser: Join a major Western Sydney civil infrastructure project delivering earthworks, roads and utilities. Strong pipeline and genuine career growth.

candidates.content_text:
Build major civil and mining infrastructure projects with a growing industry leader.
We are seeking a motivated and capable Civil Project Engineer to join our team and play a key role in delivering a diverse range of civil construction and mining projects. Working across earthworks, bulk excavation, haul roads, mine infrastructure, drainage, rehabilitation works and associated civil infrastructure, you will provide technical expertise to ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, on time, and within budget.
This is an excellent opportunity for an engineer looking to further develop their project delivery experience in a dynamic and hands-on environment.
About the Role
Reporting to the Project Manager, you will be responsible for supporting the planning, coordination and execution of civil construction projects while providing technical engineering expertise to site teams.
Key ResponsibilitiesProject Planning & Delivery
- Assist with the planning, execution and successful completion of civil construction projects.
- Develop construction methodologies, project schedules and work programs.
- Monitor project performance, identify risks and implement improvements.
- Coordinate site activities to ensure efficient project delivery.
- Support project teams in achieving production and performance targets.
Engineering & Technical Support
- Review engineering drawings, specifications and construction documentation.
- Prepare work packs, construction plans and technical reports.
- Provide technical advice and practical engineering solutions to project teams.
- Conduct site inspections to ensure works are delivered in accordance with design requirements.
- Manage design changes, technical queries and RFIs.
Quality Assurance
- Implement and maintain project quality requirements.
- Prepare inspection and test plans (ITPs) and quality documentation.
- Ensure compliance with project specifications, standards and contractual requirements.
- Manage non-conformances and corrective actions.
Health, Safety & Environment
- Champion a strong safety culture across all project sites.
- Ensure compliance with company safety systems, policies and legislative requirements.
- Participate in risk assessments, inspections and incident investigations.
- Support environmental compliance and sustainable work practices.
- Lead by example through safe and professional behaviours.
Survey & Construction Control
- Coordinate survey activities and machine control systems.
- Verify set-out, quantities and as-constructed information.
- Review survey data to ensure accuracy and compliance with project requirements.
Stakeholder Management
- Develop and maintain positive relationships with clients, subcontractors and suppliers.
- Attend project meetings and provide technical updates.
- Support Project Managers in delivering successful project outcomes.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will have:
Essential Requirements- Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering.
- Minimum 3 years' experience in civil construction, earthmoving, mining or related industries.
- Experience delivering bulk earthworks and civil infrastructure projects.
- Current Driver's Licence.
- Strong understanding of construction methodologies and project delivery processes.
- Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications and technical documentation.
- Sound knowledge of project controls and contract administration.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and project management software.
- Strong analytical, communication and problem-solving skills.
Personal Attributes- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Strong organisational and time management skills.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication abilities.
- Proactive, adaptable and solution-focused attitude.
- Genuine commitment to safety, quality and continuous improvement.
Why Join Us?
- Work on large-scale civil construction and mining projects.
- Diverse project portfolio including earthworks, mine infrastructure and rehabilitation works.
- Supportive and experienced leadership team.
- Career development and professional growth opportunities.
- Strong safety-focused culture.
- Competitive remuneration package.
Apply Now
If you're a driven Civil Project Engineer looking to advance your career with a company delivering high-profile civil and mining projects, we'd love to hear from you.
Apply today with your resume and cover letter outlining your relevant experience and project achievements.

candidates.title: 2x Undergraduate Engineer
candidates.abstract: Hall Contracting, a leading dredging and marine contractor, are looking for 2x Undergraduate Engineers to join their growing team in Sippy Downs.
bullets: Be part of a company with over 80 years civil contracting experience.
Kick off your career with this exciting opportunity.
Work in a positive workplace culture that fosters development.
candidates.content_text:
About the Company
Hall Contracting is recognised throughout Australia, the Pacific, and Asia as specialists in the dredging and marine industries. They have grown to become one of the largest contractors of their kind in Australia and consistently deliver high-quality results for their stakeholders.
With award-winning capabilities in dredging, civil contracting, and marine engineering, they pride themselves on their expertise in project management and their strong commitment to clients, employees, and the wider community.
 The Opportunity
 Hall Contracting are continuing to grow their team and are looking to take on 2x Undergraduate Engineers. You will gain invaluable engineering and construction knowledge whilst working alongside an experienced Pre-contract dredging and maritime team at our Sunshine Coast office.
 You will have an opportunity to support Hall’s preparation for a wide range of dredging and maritime projects, from small local coastal protection and beach renourishments jobs to Australia’s largest Port infrastructure developments.
 Key Responsibilities
 The responsibilities of this role will vary with the prospective projects, however we expect our undergraduates to bring their engineering and problem-solving skills to gain invaluable knowledge and then complete the following tasks:
 - Create and analyse 3D surfaces and geotechnical ground models (Civil 3D).
 - Prepare geotechnical site assessments (digitise bore logs, CPT’s and geophysical data).
 - Complete pump capacity assessments (pumping head).
 - Undertake production calculations for large dredging equipment.
 - Complete conceptual designs of marine structures.
 - Provide CAD drafting and 3D modelling services.
 - Generate and adjust delivery programs (MS Project).
 - Provide academic research and annotated bibliographies.
 - Reviewing and summarising technical documentations.
 - Complete research on construction markets.
 About You
 - Motivated to learn new things and strive for excellence in everything you do. 
 - In your 3rd year of a Bachelor’s Degree in Civil or Mechanical Engineering.
 - Possess a high level of integrity, honesty and accountability and treat everyone you encounter with utmost respect. 
 - Outstanding communication skills and ability to form strong relationships with people.
 - Available to work full-time during holiday periods.
 - Available to work 2 days a week during university periods.
Benefits
 - You will gain an understanding of construction methodologies and practices through site attendance and task observations.
 - You will gain a technical and financial acumen whilst assisting the Engineers with programmes, client and stakeholder management.
 - You may have the opportunity to work at Hall Contracting as a Graduate Engineer on the completion of your engineering degree.
 - You will work within a supportive and motivated team environment.
 - You will work for a company who creates sustainable infrastructure solutions that will be enjoyed for many generations. 
 All applications will be treated in the strictest confidence.
 Please do not hesitate to contact Aimee on 07 3041 4256 for further information or a confidential discussion.
 We look forward to speaking with you.
 Talent Blueprint partners with Hall Contracting for all recruitment matters.

candidates.content_text:
Alchemy Recruitment is partnering with a State Government client to recruit four engineering roles in Nerang, Gold Coast. You’ll join one of two teams managing more than 1,000 km of national highway and state-controlled roads across the Gold Coast, Logan and Scenic Rim. The Preservation and Maintenance team delivers maintenance, rehabilitation and road safety projects, while the Asset Management team assesses road condition and plans future works. With roles available from Student through to Principal level, this is a great opportunity to join a growing region.
 About the role
 - Pay rate of between $88.30 and $94.59 per hour + super (Principal Engineer, PO5), between $78.63 and $84.56 per hour + super (Senior Civil Engineer, PO4), between $67.95 and $74.00 per hour + super (Civil Engineer, PO3), or between $32.11 and $47.35 per hour + super (Student Engineer, PO1)
 - 12-month contracts starting early November 2026, with possible extension
 - Flexible full-time hours for the PO3, PO4 and PO5 roles; 2 to 3 days per week during semester and full-time over university breaks for the Student Engineer
 - Based at the regional office in Nerang, with regular site work across the region
 - Work on a varied program of road maintenance, pavement rehabilitation, resurfacing, bridge maintenance, asset condition assessment and road safety projects
 - Work closely with Road Operations, contractors, consultants, local councils and other government agencies
 - Contribute to safety leadership and quality outcomes on every project
 Principal Engineer (PO5) 
 - Act as Representative of the Principal for the delivery of contracts across each project phase
 - Develop contract documentation, manage tender calls and assessment (including design and construct), and lead contract award for projects in the region’s roads program
 - Project manage design and construction through the full lifecycle, including on urban and multi-lane high-speed roads
 - Report on progress and actual and forecast expenditure
 - Ensure quality and environmental requirements are identified and met
 - Supervise, allocate and mentor engineering and technical staff
 - Manage stakeholder expectations and identify political and high-risk matters early
 Senior Civil Engineer (PO4) 
 - Act as project manager and contract administrator on road projects from pre-construction through to construction
 - Manage preliminary investigations including survey, geotechnical and land resumption requirements
 - Take projects from concept design through detailed design and tender
 - Assess construction tenders, manage procurement and administer complex contracts
 - Deliver and report on Targeted Road Safety Program works and maintenance, preservation and rehabilitation programs
 - Supervise and mentor engineers, graduates and technical staff
 - Provide technical solutions during natural disaster and emergency events affecting the network
 Civil Engineer (PO3) 
 - Project manage road and bridge maintenance and rehabilitation works under the guidance of senior engineers
 - Assist in selecting the right contract model, then administer contracts through to completion
 - Set road and bridge maintenance procedures and work instructions
 - Calculate material quantities, review test results and manage non-conformances
 - Conduct risk assessments and determine construction controls
 - Inspect works and release hold points during construction and maintenance
 - Provide input into planning and design, including negotiating changes to design briefs
 Student Engineer (PO1) 
 - Join the Asset Management team under the direct supervision of a Senior Engineer
 - Investigate road asset condition and use data analytics to identify issues and solutions across the network
 - Contribute to maintenance programs and plans covering pavements, resurfacing, structures, drainage, batter slopes, heavy vehicle permits, signage and delineation
 - Assist with condition analysis and forward program preparation
 - Help prepare technical reports, stakeholder advice and replies to correspondence
 - Get out on site across the region and build practical experience alongside your studies
 Preferred Requirements 
 - Road infrastructure delivery experience at the relevant level, from state government, local council, contracting or consulting (PO3, PO4 and PO5)
 - Contract administration, superintendent or principal’s representative experience on civil works (PO3, PO4 and PO5)
 - Tender preparation and assessment experience (PO4 and PO5)
 - Experience across both pre-construction and construction phases (PO4 and PO5)
 - Leadership, supervision and mentoring of engineers (PO4 and PO5)
 - Experience on urban and multi-lane high-speed roads (PO5)
 - Materials testing review, non-conformance management and hold point release (PO3)
 - Genuine interest in road and transport infrastructure, and comfortable working with data and spreadsheets (Student Engineer)
 - Ability to commit to regular days during semester (Student Engineer)
 - Familiarity with MRTS specifications or road authority forms of contract
 - Disaster recovery or emergency works experience highly regarded
 - Sound judgement, rigorous analysis and strong stakeholder relationships
 - Clear written and verbal communication
 - Willing to undergo a criminal history check (essential, all roles)
 Preferred Qualifications 
 - Registered Professional Engineer of Queensland (RPEQ), Civil (essential for PO4 and PO5, highly regarded for PO3)
 - Four-year, Washington Accord accredited Bachelor of Engineering (Civil), or equivalent assessed by Engineers Australia (essential for PO3, PO4 and PO5)
 - Currently enrolled in second or third year of a four-year, Washington Accord accredited Bachelor of Engineering (Civil) (essential for Student Engineer)
 - Current Class C driver’s licence (essential, all roles)
 - Construction Industry Induction (White Card) (essential for PO3, PO4 and PO5)
 What’s on offer 
 - Meaningful work on a major regional road network with real ownership of projects
 - A collaborative environment with senior technical support and mentoring at every level
 - Variety across asset management, maintenance, rehabilitation, safety and emergency response work
 - For students, paid industry experience that fits around university
 - 12-month contracts with possible extension and a November start
 To apply, click Apply and attach your resume, noting which role you’re applying for. Student applicants, please also attach your academic transcript or enrolment statement. If you’re unsure which level suits your experience, apply anyway and our team will be in touch to discuss.

candidates.content_text:
Help shape stormwater’s next chapter.
You’ve built your technical skills. You’re ready to take on more responsibility, contribute your ideas and develop the confidence to lead.
Rain Consulting is looking for a Project Engineer or Scientist with 3 to 7 years’ relevant experience to join our Melbourne team.
We’re a specialist stormwater and surface water consultancy. We plan and design better water environments, investigate how water behaves and help clients turn complex information into decisions they can act on.
Our purpose
At Rain, we exist to support, challenge and lift ourselves, each other and the people we work with.
That means helping clients understand their options and giving them the clarity and confidence to act. It also means backing our own people to develop their judgement, take ownership and contribute to how the industry works.
We value creative thinking, especially when it leads to a sound, practical solution.
How we work
Our values guide our decisions and the standards we hold ourselves to:
- Quality: We check assumptions, review our work and explain the findings clearly.
- Integrity: We give honest advice, including when a client needs to hear something difficult.
- Stewardship: We consider what our decisions mean for communities and the environment over the long term.
You’ll work with major clients, including City of Melbourne and Melbourne Water, as part of a small team where your contribution is visible.
You’ll have direct support from Luke and Rianda, Rain’s Directors, and colleagues who want to see you develop. As your capability grows, there’s room to take on greater responsibility and build your own voice in the industry.
We welcome questions, thoughtful challenges and ideas for doing things better. You’ll be trusted to contribute, with technical review and support around you.
The role is Melbourne-based with hybrid working and flexibility, within a team that looks out for each other.
The problems you’ll help solve
A council is rethinking how it manages water across its community. A wetland or waterway needs a design that supports both people and the environment. A project needs a water balance to understand where water comes from, where it goes and how it could be used.
And behind each challenge, there are people who need help turning complex information into a clear way forward.
These are the kinds of questions you’ll work through at Rain.
You’ll use TUFLOW and RORB to investigate how water behaves, test options and understand their consequences. Your projects may also involve wetland and waterway design, water balances and integrated water management. You’ll turn that work into clear maps, reports and conversations that help people make sound decisions.
You’ll also get involved beyond the technical analysis. From shaping the brief to discussing the findings with the client, you’ll develop an understanding of what makes a project useful, achievable and worth doing. That includes managing scope, budgets and deadlines, with support from the team.
We want you to question assumptions and contribute ideas. If you see a better way to approach a problem, explain a result or manage water, there’s room to explore it with us.
As your confidence and capability grow, you’ll have opportunities to take greater ownership, guide others and contribute to our training or facilitation work.
The aim is for your contribution to keep helping people long after the report is delivered.
What you’ll bring
- An Engineering degree, including civil or environmental engineering, or an Environmental Science degree.
- 3 to 7 years’ relevant experience in flood, stormwater or water management.
- Solid practical TUFLOW and RORB skills.
- An understanding of hydrologic, hydraulic and stormwater processes.
- The ability to plan your work, take responsibility and ask for support when you need it.
- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain technical findings to different audiences.
- Curiosity about better ways of doing things and care for the quality and impact of your work.
Experience with MUSIC and QGIS is valuable. Training, facilitation or mentoring experience is a bonus.
Your next move
Send your CV and a short note about why you’d like to work at Rain to hiring@rainconsulting.com.au.
Tell us about the work you’ve done, the work you’d like to do next and what you’d bring to the team.
You’re also welcome to email us if you’d like to ask a question before applying.
We welcome applications from people with different backgrounds and experiences.
candidates.teaser: Project Engineer or Scientist in stormwater and water management with 3-7 years' experience. Help shape better water environments with Rain.

candidates.content_text:
CAD Drafter / Estimator
Hoardings & Temporary Works  |  Pathway to Project Management
Quick Up Hoardings  |  Pyrmont, Sydney NSW  |  Full-time 
ABOUT US:
Quick Up Hoardings is a Sydney-based specialist in certified A-Class and B-Class hoardings, overhead protective structures, laneway hoardings and bespoke structural steel solutions. We work with leading builders, developers and contractors across NSW, handling everything from site measurement and design through to engineering, fabrication and installation.
As we continue to grow, we're looking for a CAD Drafter / Estimator who wants more than a desk job. We need someone with real construction know-how who takes ownership of their work, pays close attention to detail and keeps jobs moving without needing constant direction.
THE ROLE:
You'll take projects from enquiry through to installation: attending site, measuring up, producing drawings, preparing estimates and quotes, and working directly with builders, project managers, engineers and site supervisors. You'll organise your own workload, follow up outstanding items and make sure jobs keep moving.
For the right person, there is a genuine opportunity to grow into a Project Management / Operations role as the business grows.
WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:
- Attending site to take accurate measurements and identify practical installation issues
- Understanding and explaining to clients and crews how the work will be installed
- Leading and coordinating installations when required, working alongside the crew and being prepared to assist hands-on where appropriately trained and competent
- Preparing AutoCAD 2D drawings and site layouts for A-Class and B-Class hoardings and temporary structures
- Preparing workshop drawings showing what needs to be made, including measurements, materials and cutting lengths where required
- Reading and interpreting architectural, structural, civil and survey drawings
- Preparing material and labour take-offs
- Estimating labour, steel, timber, transport, crane/HIAB, EWP, engineering, installation and dismantle
- Obtaining prices from suppliers and subcontractors when needed
- Preparing quotations and detailed scopes of work
- Preparing drawings to meet SafeWork NSW Codes of Practice, Australian Standards and council requirements, including clearances, pedestrian protection, access and structural arrangements
- Supporting council submissions and reviewing the specific requirements of different NSW councils, including City of Sydney Type-A and Type-B hoarding requirements
- Managing multiple projects, following up outstanding items and keeping jobs moving from enquiry to installation
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR:
Essential
- Practical, hands-on site experience: you can take accurate measurements, identify installation issues, and understand and explain how the work will be installed
- Hands-on leadership and practical site capability: able to confidently run or coordinate an installation, understand the work being carried out, and lead by example when required
- Strong AutoCAD 2D drafting skills
- Ability to use SolidWorks or similar 3D software (you don't need to be an expert in 3D modelling)
- Ability to prepare workshop drawings for fabrication, including measurements, materials and cutting lengths
- Estimating experience, including obtaining supplier and subcontractor pricing
- Solid understanding of structural steel, beams, posts, baseplates, bracing, timber framing, plywood, gates and connections
- Strong initiative and ownership: able to organise your workload, follow up outstanding items and keep jobs moving without constant direction
- Strong attention to detail
- Confidence dealing directly with builders, project managers, engineers and site supervisors
- Knowledge of, or the ability to quickly get across, the SafeWork NSW Overhead Protective Structures Code of Practice (commenced 12 December 2025), relevant Australian Standards and council requirements
- Good Excel skills
- Current driver licence
Preferred
- Ideally 5+ years of relevant experience in structural steel, scaffolding, temporary works, hoardings, façade, architectural metalwork or similar construction
- NSW construction experience
Please note: This role is not suited to someone who has only worked behind a desk producing drawings. We need someone who is comfortable on site and understands how the job actually gets built.
WHAT WE OFFER
- An opportunity to grow into a Project Management / Operations role as the business grows
- Ownership of projects from start to finish
- Varied work across commercial, residential and mixed-use developments in Sydney and NSW
- A growing business where initiative is noticed and rewarded
- [Salary/vehicle / other benefits TBD]

candidates.content_text:
About Us
 Aquirian Limited (ASX: AQN) is a leading provider of people, equipment and technology solutions to the mining and resources sector. Through our specialised businesses, including Maglok, we develop and deliver innovative products and services that help our clients operate more safely, efficiently and profitably.
 At Maglok, innovation drives everything we do. We design, manufacture and continuously improve products that solve real operational challenges faced by defence and mining companies across Australia.
 About the Role
 This is an exciting opportunity to become part of a dynamic defence and mining technology business that develops practical, innovative solutions for the defence, mining and resources industry. You'll play a key role in the design, development, testing and implementation of products and technologies that improve safety, productivity and operational performance for our clients.
 Reporting to the Operations Manager, this position will work closely with our workshop team to deliver design, drafting and engineering support across a range of standard and custom projects.
 You will be responsible for assisting the Operations Manager and workshop team with mechanical design and drafting, developing specialised tooling and workshop improvements, supporting product development initiatives, and contributing to automation projects that will shape the future of mining technology.
 This role also includes responsibility for managing the small workshop stores area, including stocktakes, inventory control and material management.
 While design governance and support will be available from Aquirian's Engineering Team in Perth, this role is intended to operate with a high degree of autonomy and ownership. We are looking for someone who can identify opportunities, solve problems, and drive projects from concept through to implementation.
 Key Responsibilities
 - Produce 2D & 3D CAD models, engineering drawings and technical documentation.
 - Provide design and drafting support for standard and custom engineering projects.
 - Design specialised tooling, workshop equipment and continuous improvement initiatives.
 - Support concept development, product design, prototyping and testing activities.
 - Assist with manufacturing, fabrication and design review processes.
 - Prepare technical reports, specifications and engineering documentation.
 - Support prototype builds, product validation and field-testing activities.
 - Assist with inventory management, stock control and workshop stores administration.
 - Assist with QA/QC on ongoing jobs, safety developments and implementation of SWMS, work instructions.
 - Contribute to workshop efficiency, safety and continuous improvement projects.
 - Undertake additional duties and projects as directed by the Operations Manager
 About You
 You are an energetic, self-motivated and technically capable Mechanical Designer or Engineer who enjoys working in a practical environment.
 You will bring a strong foundation in mechanical design, excellent problem-solving abilities and a genuine desire to learn, innovate and contribute as part of a collaborative team.
 Essential Requirements
 - Degree or Diploma in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline.
 - Experience in mechanical design and drafting.
 - Proficiency in Autodesk Inventor and AutoCAD.
 - Strong understanding of mechanical design principles and manufacturing processes.
 - Experience producing engineering drawings and technical documentation.
 - Strong technical, analytical and problem-solving skills.
 - Ability to work autonomously and manage competing priorities.
 - Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
 - Commitment to safety, quality and continuous improvement.
 - Positive attitude with a willingness to learn and contribute.
 Desirable Experience
 - Mining, manufacturing or fabrication industry experience.
 - Finite Element Analysis (FEA) experience.
 - Product development, prototyping and testing experience.
 - Workshop, fabrication or practical manufacturing experience.
 - Inventory management or workshop stores experience.
 Why Join Maglok?
 This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing Australian mining technology company and contribute to the development of innovative products used throughout the resources sector.
 We Offer
 ✅ Competitive salary package
 ✅ Supportive and collaborative environment
 ✅ Modern workshop facilities located in Lonsdale, SA
 ✅ Hands-on involvement from concept design through to implementation
 ✅ The opportunity to deliver real productivity gains and cost savings for mining clients
 Apply Now
 If you're looking for a role where you can apply your engineering expertise, drive innovation and make a genuine impact on the future of mining technology, we would love to hear from you.
 Submit your resume and a brief cover letter outlining your experience and suitability for the role.
 SAFE SPACES
 To Speak • To Work • To Live
BE BOLD
 With Thinking • With innovation • With Solutions
OWN OUTCOMES
 Define it • Plan it • Do it
SHARED SUCCESS
 Work together • Create together • Win together

candidates.content_text:
Graduate Structural Engineer | Remedial Consultancy | Pyrmont
Job Summary
Join a growing Sydney engineering consultancy specialising in remedial, structural and façade engineering. An excellent opportunity for a Civil Engineering graduate with an interest in structures to gain practical experience, work alongside experienced engineers and develop their career.
About the Business
Our client is a well-established and growing engineering consultancy based in Pyrmont, specialising in remedial engineering, façade remediation and structural rehabilitation projects.
The business has developed a strong reputation through its technical expertise and long-standing client relationships, working across residential, commercial and government projects.
Their portfolio includes remedial, façade and structural rehabilitation projects ranging from approximately $2 million to $15 million+, providing excellent exposure to different buildings, structural systems and engineering challenges.
With continued growth, they're looking to appoint a Graduate Engineer who can develop alongside their experienced engineering team.
The Opportunity
This is an excellent opportunity for a recent Civil Engineering graduate who has a particular interest in structural engineering and wants to develop their technical skills within a consultancy environment.
You'll work closely with experienced engineers, gaining exposure to building inspections, structural investigations, defect assessments, remedial design and construction.
Rather than being limited to office-based design work, you'll have the opportunity to develop an understanding of how buildings perform, why defects occur and how practical engineering solutions are developed and implemented.
The business is looking for someone with a great attitude, strong willingness to learn and genuine ambition to build a long-term career in engineering.
Key Responsibilities
- Assist senior engineers with structural and remedial engineering projects
- Support building inspections, site investigations and defect assessments
- Assist with structural assessments and engineering calculations
- Support the preparation of technical reports and remedial scopes of work
- Assist with structural and remedial design documentation
- Coordinate with engineers, consultants and contractors
- Attend site inspections and develop practical construction knowledge
- Support project delivery and maintain accurate technical documentation
About You
You'll ideally have:
- Completed Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering
- Ideally 1-2 years post graduate experience
- A strong interest in structural engineering, ideally with relevant structural subjects or project experience
- Good understanding of structural engineering fundamentals
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
- Excellent attention to detail
- Good written and verbal communication skills
- Positive attitude and willingness to learn
- Professional, personable and proactive approach
- Genuine interest in remedial engineering and building structures
Previous internship or work experience within structural engineering, construction or building consultancy would be advantageous but isn't essential.
Recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Attitude, communication and willingness to develop are particularly important.
What's in it for you?
- Join an established and growing engineering consultancy
- Learn directly from experienced structural and remedial engineers
- Exposure to building defects, structural investigations and remedial design
- Opportunity to gain both office-based and practical site experience
- Diverse projects across residential and commercial buildings
- Supportive, collaborative team environment
- Genuine opportunity to develop your technical capability and progress within the business
- Convenient Pyrmont location, close to Sydney CBD
If you're a Civil Engineering graduate with an interest in structural engineering and are looking for an opportunity to learn from experienced engineers and build a long-term career, we'd be keen to hear from you.
Apply via SEEK, email mike@daviesrossconsulting.com.au or contact Michael Forshaw on 0401 724 180 for a confidential discussion.

Most students finish their degree and diploma and then go looking for experience. Our cadets finish with two years of it done and a launch into their career.

Through three structured rotations, you'll gain exposure to different aspects of the business, work alongside experienced industry professionals and discover where your strengths and interests lie.

Who We're Looking For
We're seeking graduates who are excited about building a career in construction and ready to gain hands-on experience.

 - Project Management
 - Estimating or Quantity Surveying

candidates.title: Production Draftsperson
candidates.abstract: Ready for more than standard floor plans? Work on a wider range of residential projects than you would with most builders.
bullets: Work on a different kind of project almost every week
Have a voice in a close-knit team that values your expertise
Be part of a team that make a real difference to people’s lives.
screening_questions: Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
How many years' experience do you have as a Production Draftsperson?
How much notice are you required to give your current employer?
candidates.content_text:
Why work with Goldstate Homes
At Goldstate Homes, we build across a wider range of residential markets than most builders: investment homes, knockdown rebuilds, dual occupancies, townhouses, SDA homes, co-living properties, Class 1b rooming houses, dual key homes and turnkey house and land packages. For our team, that means varied and challenging work. No two projects are quite the same, and you'll keep building your skills and experience across many building types. We pride ourselves on speed, service and quality, and we build every home as if it were our own. Our people take real ownership of their work and can see what they've contributed to every home we deliver. If you want to grow your career in a close-knit team that cares about doing things properly, Goldstate Homes is a great place to be.
The role
We're looking for an experienced Production Draftsperson to join the team. Reporting to the Drafting Manager, you'll prepare detailed, accurate working drawings from our current portfolio and custom homes. You'll take each job from sales plans through to construction-ready documentation.
Your day-to-day will include:
- Preparing production and working drawings in Revit.
- Applying client variations, site-specific changes, engineering and developer requirements to drawings
- Checking that plans comply with the NCC, council and regulatory body requirements
- Working with our BDM, Estimating, Contract Admin and Construction teams to provide technical support for client and agent queries
- Liaising with Building Surveyors, Engineers, Councils and Town Planners
- Keeping templates, standards and drawing sets consistent and up to date
About you
- At least 3 years' demonstrated experience as a production draftsperson in volume or custom residential building
- A thorough working knowledge of the NCC and residential construction methods
- Intermediate to advanced Revit skills (essential)
- Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy
- Good problem-solving skills and the ability to find practical solutions
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- Ability to manage your workload and meet deadlines
- A team player who does well in a supportive, close-knit environment
What we offer
- Working with a friendly, close-knit team where your contribution is valued
- Varied work across both volume and custom residential projects
- Support and guidance from an experienced Drafting Manager
- Opportunities for professional development and career growth
- Be part of an established and growing residential building company
- A competitive salary
candidates.teaser: Ready for more than standard floor plans? Work on a wider range of residential projects than you would with most builders.

candidates.title: Water and Sewer Operations Trainee
candidates.abstract: Join Council's Emerging Talent Program and gain hands-on experience in water and sewer services while completing a Certificate III qualification.
candidates.location: Bega, Wollongong, Illawarra & South Coast NSW
bullets: Gain a nationally recognised qualification while you work.
Build practical skills across water, sewer and network operations.
Launch your career through Council's Emerging Talent Program.
candidates.content_text:
A career with Bega Valley Shire Council offers the opportunity to engage in meaningful and diverse work that supports the vibrant communities of the south-east corner of NSW. Nestled between rolling hills and some of the state’s most stunning beaches, this region is home to a variety of people who enjoy both rural and coastal living.
As an AR Bluett Award winning Council, we are proud of our dedicated and talented team, whose efforts make our success possible.
With a workforce of over 350, we provide essential services to our communities, including libraries, customer service, finance, children’s services, engineering, project management, road maintenance, water management, environment, parks, gardens, and town centres.
We offer a range of employment benefits to support our staff, which may include:
 - Rostered days off
 - Flexible work arrangements
 - Salary packaging
 - Paid study leave of 3 hours per week (or equivalent over a four-week period)
 - Approved study-related expenses
 The Opportunity
We have an exciting opportunity for a motivated individual to join Councils Emerging Talent Program and undertake a Certificate III in Water Industry Operations while gaining practical experience and mentorship across Council's Water and Sewer Services.
As a Water and Sewer Trainee, you will combine vocational studies with hands-on workplace experience across a range of water and sewer network operations functions, including Water Treatment Operations, Sewerage Treatment Operations, Network Maintenance, and Infrastructure Construction. You will gain practical experience in the operation, monitoring and maintenance of essential water and sewer services while developing the skills, knowledge and qualifications required for a rewarding career in the water industry.
The role may also involve travel and participation in residential training blocks associated with your qualification program.
As a participant in Council's Emerging Talent Program, you will have the opportunity to develop your skills through structured learning, on-the-job experience, mentoring and exposure to a broad range of professional disciplines, building a strong foundation for a successful career in local government and beyond.
Council will support your studies by providing paid study leave of 3 hours per week (or equivalent over a four-week period) together with approved study-related expenses.
Key responsibilities include:
 - Undertake vocational studies and apply theoretical learning to workplace activities to develop practical skills and knowledge.
 - Assist with the operation, monitoring and maintenance of water and sewerage infrastructure and associated systems.
 - Assist in the construction, installation and repair of water supply and sewerage infrastructure.
 - Assist with the maintenance, servicing and cleaning of water and sewer treatment plant and equipment.
 - Develop skills in inspection, fault finding, testing and problem solving across water and sewer networks.
 This role offers valuable exposure to a broad range of water and sewer operations while developing practical skills and experience to support a future career in Water and Sewer Services.
To view the Position Description, please click here. 
About You
We are seeking two (2) individuals who have obtained a School Certificate (Year 10) or equivalent and hold a NSW Class C drivers' licence (or ability to obtain).
You will have the following skills and experience;
 - Demonstrated analytical and investigative ability to assist in resolving operational problems in the field.
 - Ability to participate in the laying, repair and maintenance of water and sewer mains and associated construction activities.
 - Ability to develop fault-finding and troubleshooting skills relevant to water supply and sewerage systems.
 - Well-developed oral and written communication skills.
 - Demonstrated commitment to learning, teamwork and working safely in an operational environment.
 Benefits
This is a fixed term full-time position working 38 hours per week for a period of two (2) years.
The total remuneration package for this position commences at $29,195.71 to $50,115.52 gross per annum, comprising of:
 - $501.30 to 860.50 per week base salary
 - $60.16 to 860.50 per week superannuation (calculated at 12%)
 Remuneration for this position is dependent upon the age and level of schooling achieved by the successful candidate.
Additional benefits for this position include:
 - Rostered day off scheme (nine day fortnight)
 - Paid study leave of up to 3 hours per week (or equivalent over a four-week period)
 - Approved study-related expenses
 - Annual Award salary increases and performance reviews
 - Salary packaging program (SmartSalary)
 - Wellbeing Initiatives – Fitness Passport, Employee Assistance Program, Telus Health App, social club, health monitoring and annual flu vaccinations
 For further information on this position, please contact Luke Cathor - Water and Sewer Networks Operations Coordinator on 0467 787 467.
Applications close 11.59pm AEDT on 22 November 2026.
Applicants must have the right to work in Australia and address the advertised selection criteria demonstrating their suitability for the role.
This position requires applicants to be suitably immunised in line with recommendations from the Australian Immunisation Handbook, mandated Public Health Orders and/or Councils Immunisation Procedure.

candidates.title: Construction Cadet
candidates.abstract: Keen to kick start your career in the Construction Industry and work alongside your degree? Apply now we're keen to hear from you!
bullets: Part-time and Full-time opportunities
Earn while you learn
Experience a variety of career pathways
candidates.content_text:
Building for Generations through the Pursuit of Excellence
The FKG Construction team has a proud 50+ year history of successfully delivering a variety of commercial construction projects across a wide range of sectors including both government and private clients. We are dedicated to building for generations, achieved through our personable approach with all people, including those within our communities within which we live every day.
We believe our people are the key to our success and we are invested in supporting the wellbeing of our team members, providing skills development opportunities, rewarding performance and recognising high achievement.
As an FKG Group employee you will have access to our range of benefits which includes corporate health insurance discounts, employee assistance program, our “Thrive” wellbeing initiative and many more.
The Role
Keen to kick start your career in the construction industry and work alongside your degree? Then look no further!  Due to recent organisational growth we are looking for our next superstar Cadet!
A cadetship at FKG will give you knowledge across all areas of construction, you'll learn from experienced members of the team, obtain hands-on involvement across a variety of exciting commercial projects and be given excellent learning support and mentorship as you develop your career.
Responsibilities
You will enjoy the variety within your job scope, including:
- Organisation and management of suppliers and subcontractors
- Procurement of trade packages and assistance in developing cost reports;
- Liaison with clients, site staff, design managers, estimators, and project managers
- Estimation, design and contract administration
Experience and Qualifications
 To be considered for this role, you will need:
- To be currently enrolled and successfully completed the first year of your Bachelor of Construction Management/ Urban Development/ Quantity Surveying
- Highly developed organisational, time management and prioritising skills A can-do attitude, self-motivated and willingness to learn;
- An exceptional level of verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills Previous construction industry experience would be an advantage;
- To include your ATAR results on your resume.
Apply Now!
- FKG is an equal opportunity employer, where we recognise the diversity of our team and actively promote equality of opportunity for all with the right mix of talent, skills and potential. We welcome all applications from a wide range of candidates. Selection for roles will be based on individual merit alone. 
- Apply with “Quick Apply” or email hr@fkg.com.au with your CV.

candidates.title: Estimator
candidates.abstract: Crucial role in the continued success of UGL Regional Linx safely operating and maintaining the Country Regional Network in regional NSW
candidates.location: Bathurst, Blue Mountains & Central West NSW
bullets: Historic piece of regional NSW rail infrastructure
Excellent long term career prospects
Work in a motivated, inclusive, high performing and flexible environment
candidates.content_text:
About UGL Regional Linx
At UGL Regional Linx (UGLRL), we help connect communities across regional New South Wales by managing and maintaining the Country Regional Network (CRN). As a subsidiary of UGL Transport, we are proud to create meaningful employment opportunities in regional and rural communities, with more than 85% of our workforce based across regional NSW.
We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where people feel valued, supported, and empowered to succeed. Guided by our core values, we foster a culture built on collaboration, respect, safety, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Job Purpose
The Estimator is responsible for preparing project estimates with accurate cost allocations and up to date market knowledge, monitoring the performance of project estimates, managing the change control process associated with project estimates, maintaining the CATS Resource Library with current benchmarked rates, and leading the overall 3MWP estimation process with the support of Infrastructure delivery team subject matter experts, the Procurement team, Finance team, and Assets & Engineering subject matter experts. 
The Estimator supports Project Owners by preparing and updating cost estimates for variations and facilitating the conversion of provisional sums to fixed-cost submissions.
What You'll Be Doing
Be responsible for the estimation of the 3 Year Maintenance Works Program, including the supervision and management of external and internal resources used during the process of estimation
Prepare detailed estimates for every project in the 3MWP in line with the Project Controls Plan process for estimation.
Assist in the preparation of UGLRL Enhancements estimates as required, including the loading of those estimates into CATS
Preparing and updating Estimates for Variations and conversion of Provisional Sum to Fixed Costs submissions
Maintain the UGL Regional Linx CATS Register and Master Resource Library
Maintain up to date Labour, Plant, Material rates within the Master Resource Library
Develop and maintain an “Estimating Manual” for UGLRL Projects. 
Review all project documentation to understand the requirements of the work to include the analysis of technical, contractual and financial requirements.
Explore opportunities for innovation while identifying risk and opportunities.
Maintain accurate and details estimate files.
Maintain awareness of best practice in the industry
Develop innovative estimates and options through knowledge of the latest design and or construction techniques to deliver the best possible outcome for UGLRL
Coordinates and collaborates with subject matter experts on methodology, program, IR, Plant and estimate review processes
Perform trend analysis and actively evaluate project cost and estimate performance
About You
Tertiary qualification in Engineering, Quantity Surveying or similar profession. (Desirable)
3+ years’ experience working in an estimating role
Knowledge of construction, material components, regulations and estimating
Sound knowledge and experience within the rail industry, especially in an O&M context
Ability to read and interpret drawings/plans and specifications
Why Join UGL Regional Linx?
Be part of an organisation that plays a vital role in connecting regional communities.
Work within a supportive and collaborative team environment.
Access opportunities for professional growth and career development.
Contribute to projects with lasting community and infrastructure impact.
Join a business that values diversity, inclusion, and different perspectives.
Diversity & Inclusion
At UGL Regional Linx, we believe diverse teams create better outcomes. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities.
We are particularly committed to increasing female representation across our business and strongly encourage women to apply, even if you don't meet every requirement listed.
We also encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people living with disability, culturally and linguistically diverse candidates, LGBTQIA+ individuals, and mature-age professionals.
Our recruitment process may include national criminal history checks and pre-employment medical assessments, including drug and alcohol screening.

Coordinate stakeholders to ensure safe, compliant project outcomes.
Deliver projects on time, within budget, and to quality standards.
candidates.content_text:
Company description:
STERIS is a leading provider of infection prevention and procedural products and services, focused primarily on the critical markets of healthcare, pharmaceutical and research and medical devices. Our mission is to help our Customers create a healthier and safer world by providing innovative healthcare and life science product and service solutions around the globe. We have 12,000 employees worldwide, with over 3,000 in Customer-facing sales and service roles. Founded as Innovative Medical Technologies in Ohio in 1985, the company was renamed STERIS in 1987. Many of the businesses that have been acquired and integrated into STERIS have much longer operating histories, notably the American Sterilizer Company founded in 1894. The STERIS Vision is inspired by our Customers' efforts to create a healthier and safer world, and guided by our legacy of leadership and innovation; we strive to be a Great Company. To STERIS, this means we will make a difference by providing world-class product and service solutions for our Customers, safe and rewarding work for our People, and superior returns for our Shareholders.
Job description:
Position Summary
As a Project Engineer, you will play a key role in delivering exceptional customer outcomes through the design, coordination, and end-to-end execution of capital medical equipment projects across the STERIS Healthcare portfolio throughout Australia and New Zealand. From initial project scoping and design development through to installation, commissioning, and project completion, you will ensure projects are delivered safely, on time, within budget, and in compliance with clinical and regulatory requirements.
Working collaboratively with Sales, Project Managers, Installation Teams, Clinical Stakeholders, Consultants, Contractors, and Vendors, you will provide technical expertise, design guidance, and project coordination across multiple healthcare facilities and technologies. This role is ideal for a proactive engineering professional who thrives in a customer-focused environment and is passionate about delivering high-quality healthcare solutions while upholding STERIS's commitment to safety, quality, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence.
What You Will Do
 * Define project scope, objectives, milestones, and deliverables aligned with customer and business requirements.
 * Provide design, planning, and coordination of CSD, Endo and Surgical projects from pre-sales through to installation and project closeout.
 * Develop equipment layouts, specifications, CAD & REVIT drawings, sizing reports, schedules, budgets, quotations, and technical proposals.
 * Review project requirements, drawings, and specifications to ensure compliance with healthcare standards and best practices.
 * Develop and maintain project plans, tracking scope, schedule, cost, quality, and resource requirements.
 * Provide technical expertise during customer presentations, design workshops, and tender submissions.
 * Coordinate customers, consultants, contractors, vendors, and internal stakeholders to ensure successful project delivery.
 * Prepare and manage project budgets, quotations, and tender responses within approved financial targets.
 * Monitor project progress, quality, and safety performance in accordance with STERIS standards and quality management systems
 * Identify, assess, and manage project risks, issues, and change controls throughout the project lifecycle.
 * Build and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, including architects, builders, consultants, and clinical teams.
 * Support continuous improvement initiatives and contribute to LEAN, 5S, Sustainability, and One Team One Goal objectives.
 * Provide National Installation Coordinator coverage during periods of leave.
 * Promote and uphold STERIS values, culture, safety, quality, and customer satisfaction in all activities.
The Experience, Skills and Abilities Needed
Required:
 * Bachelor's Degree in Engineering.
 * Proficient in CAD and/or REVIT drafting packages.
 * Good understanding of CSD Standards e.g. AS 5369:2023.
 * Demonstrated experience delivering complex projects, preferably within healthcare, medical devices, capital equipment, engineering, construction, or technical environments.
 * Valid driver's licence and willingness to travel as required.
Preferred:
 * Project Management experience.
 * Experience working with healthcare facility projects, sterilisation departments, operating theatres, or medical capital equipment installations.
 * Knowledge of quality management systems and continuous improvement methodologies.
Others:
 * Strong project planning and organisational skills.
 * Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
 * Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building capability.
 * Commercial awareness and budget management skills.
 * Ability to assess and mitigate project risks.
 * Customer-focused mindset with a commitment to delivering exceptional service.
 * High attention to detail and quality standards.
 * Ability to remain calm under pressure and make sound decisions

About the Client
 Our client is an established technology organisation delivering secure infrastructure solutions across Defence, government and critical infrastructure environments. They offer a highly technical and collaborative workplace, with a strong focus on professional development, industry certifications and long-term career growth.
 About the Role
 We are seeking an experienced Infrastructure Engineer to help build, maintain and support secure, bare-metal infrastructure within disconnected environments.
 The role will involve working across Linux, Kubernetes, server, storage, networking and firewall technologies. You will support both new infrastructure deployments and the ongoing operation of the environment, including incident response, troubleshooting, patching and hardware maintenance. 
 Key responsibilities will include:
- Deploying and managing Kubernetes clusters on bare-metal infrastructure
- Administering Linux systems across build, patching and operational activities
- Troubleshooting infrastructure issues across hardware, Linux, Kubernetes and network layers
- Completing firmware updates and offline patching within secure environments
- Configuring and supporting server, storage, network and firewall components
- Maintaining clear technical documentation, build records and operational procedures
- Working with internal engineers, vendors and delivery partners to achieve agreed outcomes  
The role is primarily based on-site within a secure facility. Depending on operational requirements, some positions may involve participation in a rotating shift roster, including work outside standard business hours.
 The Successful Candidate
 To be successful, you will have:
- Strong Linux system administration and troubleshooting skills
- Practical experience deploying or supporting Kubernetes on bare-metal infrastructure
- Sound networking knowledge and experience using Linux networking tools
- Experience with out-of-band management and serial console access
- An understanding of working within air-gapped or offline environments
- Experience with Git and version-controlled technical environments
- Scripting or automation experience using Bash, Python or Ansible
- Hands-on experience with at least one of the following:- HPE server infrastructure
- NetApp storage technologies
- Cisco switching
- Palo Alto Networks firewalls
Experience with PKI, certificate management, service mesh technologies or highly secure government environments will be highly regarded. Relevant certifications across Kubernetes, Linux, networking, storage or security technologies would also be beneficial. 
 What is on Offer
- A long-term, full-time opportunity
- Exposure to complex and highly secure infrastructure environments
- Support for relevant professional training and certifications
- The opportunity to broaden your skills across Linux, Kubernetes, networking, storage and security technologies
- A supportive technical team focused on knowledge sharing and professional development
- Meaningful work supporting critical Australian technology environments
Location: Canberra, ACT – onsite/hybrid option available
 Security Requirements: To be eligible for this role, you must be an Australian Citizen. Due to the work environment, our client has requested that all candidates are required to hold current NV2 Security Clearance.
 How to Apply: 
Please upload your resume to apply. Please note you will need to complete selection criteria to complete this application process. We will be in touch with instructions for suitably skilled candidates.
Applications open until 23 October 2026
 Candidates will need to be willing to undergo pre-employment screening checks which may include, ID and work rights, security clearance verification and any other client requested checks.

• A small office team supporting a substantial site workforce

You won't just be sitting behind a desk running CAD software—you will spend significant time on the floor coordinating production, managing inventory and ERP systems, solving assembly bottlenecks, and helping us continuously improve how we build.

About You

candidates.title: Estimator
candidates.abstract: In this role, you will effectively  support the preparation of accurate cost estimates for tender submissions and ongoing projects.
candidates.content_text:
Company description:
Clough is a pioneering project delivery company. We harness innovative engineering and construction solutions to improve peoples' lives today and tomorrow.
We deliver large, complex projects for the infrastructure, energy, and resources industries, underpinned by a dedication to innovation, sustainability and getting the job done safely and efficiently. 
Our business is built on a foundation of strong values, earning us a respected reputation as an employer of a diverse and talented workforce who share in our passion for projects.
We are committed to providing our people with opportunities to learn, grow and thrive. By investing in their careers, we are not only supporting the growth of the engineering and construction industries, but ensuing Australia is well-positioned to deliver the nation-building projects that will enable a more sustainable future.
Job description:
We build careers. 
Long-term project opportunities available 
Opportunity to work on a major infrastructure project in Sydney/Melbourne/Brisbane 
Pioneering project delivery company 
We have an exciting opportunity for an Estimator to join the Bidding Team in Sydney, Melbourne or Brisbane! In this role, you will effectively support the preparation of accurate cost estimates for tender submissions and ongoing projects.
Who we are
Webuild in Australia is comprised of Webuild, Clough and e2o. Together, we are a pioneering project delivery company. We harness innovative engineering and construction solutions to improve peoples' lives today and tomorrow.
We deliver large, complex projects for the infrastructure, energy, and resources industries, underpinned by a dedication to innovation, sustainability and getting the job done safely and efficiently. 
Our business is built on a foundation of strong values, earning us a respected reputation as an employer of a diverse and talented workforce who share in our passion for projects.
We are committed to providing our people with opportunities to learn, grow and thrive. By investing in their careers, we are not only supporting the growth of the engineering and construction industries, but ensuing Australia is well-positioned to deliver the nation-building projects that will enable a more sustainable future.
Who you are
Innovative. Curious. Passionate. Creative. These are just a few words that describe you.
Your focus will include:
 - Assist in preparing cost plans, tender submissions, and accurate direct and indirect cost estimates for construction and infrastructure projects. 
 - Review project documentation, drawings, specifications, and scopes of work to determine estimating requirements and support estimate development. 
 - Gather, analyse, and maintain cost, productivity, and market pricing data, while liaising with suppliers and subcontractors to obtain pricing and technical information. 
 - Support tender activities by assisting with supplier quote evaluations, risk assessments, cost reviews, and the preparation of rates, qualifications, and clarifications. 
 - Collaborate with project teams and senior estimators to ensure estimates are completed accurately, comply with company procedures, and contribute to successful tender outcomes. 
What you will bring to the team:
 - Tertiary qualification in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management or a related discipline, or currently working towards completion.
 - Demonstrated experience in the building, engineering, construction or infrastructure industry.
 - Previous experience in an estimating, project controls, engineering or related project support role is desirable.
 - Developing knowledge of tender preparation, cost estimating and project delivery processes.
 - Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, and the ability to learn and utilise estimating software.
 - Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications and scopes of work.
 - Strong analytical, numerical and problem-solving skills with a high level of attention to detail.
 - Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams.
 - Understanding of, or willingness to develop knowledge of, first-principles estimating, productivity factors and cost benchmarking techniques.
 - Experience within the building, engineering, construction or infrastructure sectors will be highly regarded.
Clough's people enjoy:
 - A competitive remuneration package
 - Industry leading paid parental leave program from the day you join 
 - Flexible and remote work options to manage work and lifestyle commitments 
 - Ongoing learning and development opportunities (through Engineers Australia, AIM Training, LinkedIn Learning and more) 
 - Numerous mental health and well-being programs  
 - Special offers on private health insurance, salary packaging, banking, retail and more 
 - Exposure to a range of iconic projects and industries   
 - Salary continuance insurance (criteria applies) 
We're building a diverse workforce
We are committed to building a workforce that reflects the communities in which we work and live, fostering an inclusive environment that accepts every person, embraces their strengths and differences, and provides opportunities for all to achieve their full potential.
We are a certified Employer of Choice for Gender Equality by the Workplace Gender Equality Agency, a WORK180 Endorsed Employer for All Women, a signatory of the Veterans' Employment Commitment, a partner of Pride in Diversity as LGBTQIA+ allies, and an active member of CEOs for Gender Equity. Guided by our Reconciliation Action Plan, we are committed to providing meaningful training and employment opportunities to deliver positive outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples. 
As an employer of choice, we strongly encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including women, veterans, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, and candidates with culturally diverse backgrounds.
Apply now to join us!
Once we receive your application, it will be reviewed for shortlisting. Should your application be shortlisted we will contact you.
Please note: We reserve the right to commence the shortlisting process for this role immediately and the right to remove the advertisement before the closing date. Agency submissions will not be considered for this position.

candidates.title: SMP Project Engineer
candidates.abstract: Monadelphous looking for an experienced Project Engineer – SMP in QLD.
candidates.content_text:
Monadelphous is continuing to grow, and we're looking for an experienced SMP Project Engineer to join our Engineering Construction division on a major energy infrastructure project in regional Queensland.
Located in Chinchilla, Queensland, this is a 2:1 roster role and an excellent opportunity to join an experienced project team delivering structural, mechanical and piping (SMP) construction works for a major energy company.
Working closely with the project, engineering and construction teams, you'll play a key role in the planning, coordination and delivery of SMP works, supporting the successful execution of a major energy infrastructure project.
Working with Monadelphous offers many benefits, some of which include:
- Work on a major energy infrastructure project in regional Queensland
- 2:1 DIDO roster from Brisbane
- Long-term career opportunities within Monadelphous' Engineering Construction division
- Exposure to multidisciplinary engineering, construction and project delivery teams
- Professional development and mentoring from experienced leaders
- Opportunity to work on complex SMP construction activities within the energy sector
Key Responsibilities
- Support the planning, coordination and delivery of SMP construction activities to achieve project objectives.
- Coordinate engineering and construction interfaces to ensure works are delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with project requirements.
- Prepare and manage construction documentation including work packs, technical queries, RFIs, ITPs and quality documentation.
- Coordinate procurement activities, material requirements and subcontractor interfaces.
- Monitor project progress and assist with planning, scheduling, forecasting and reporting activities.
- Review engineering deliverables and ensure construction activities are aligned with approved drawings, specifications and project requirements.
- Liaise with construction teams, project personnel, client representatives, subcontractors and other key stakeholders to support successful project delivery.
- Assist with identifying and resolving technical, construction and project issues.
- Support project cost control, change management and commercial reporting activities.
- Promote safe work practices and ensure compliance with project specifications, quality requirements and Monadelphous standards.
- Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives across project engineering and construction delivery.
What You'll Bring
- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Civil or related Engineering discipline.
- Demonstrated experience in a Project Engineer role delivering SMP construction projects within the energy, resources, mining, oil & gas or heavy industrial sectors.
- Strong understanding of SMP construction methodologies, engineering interfaces and QA/QC processes.
- Experience with construction documentation including work packs, ITPs, RFIs, technical queries and engineering deliverables.
- Strong organisational and communication skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders and manage competing priorities.
- Commercial awareness and an understanding of project cost, schedule and change management.
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and relevant project management systems.
- Australian working rights.
- Current Australian driver's licence and 
- Willingness to work a 2:1 roster 
Life at Monadelphous
There’s lots to get involved in, celebratory or cultural events and so much more. We work hard to make Monadelphous a truly great place to work.
We celebrate our diversity and shared values and are committed to inclusion and equal opportunities for all. We’re committed to hiring locally, encourage people of all diverse backgrounds to apply and strongly encourage women and First Nations people to submit an application.
About us
Monadelphous is an ASX-200 company providing multidisciplinary construction, maintenance and industrial services to many of the largest companies in the resources, energy and infrastructure sectors. Established in 1972, we’ve been working in Australia and around the world for more than 50 years. We work on the biggest projects and ensure our teams have a variety of opportunities available to follow their career path of choice.
Our Engineering Construction division is an increasingly diverse business, focusing on managing and delivering large-scale project management and construction services. Our expertise includes civil construction, structural steel fabrication, modularisation and delivery, as well as structural, mechanical, piping and tank construction. We also specialise in heavy lift and haulage services, electrical and instrumentation work and renewable energy infrastructure.
Safety is at the forefront of everything we do, and we live by our promise: The Safe Way is the Only Way. Apply now to get started. A career at Monadelphous is a career with a difference. Make it yours.
candidates.teaser: Monadelphous looking for an experienced Project Engineer – SMP in QLD.
