candidates.title: Site Engineer
candidates.abstract: We are seeking a detail driven Site Engineer to lead quality through to finishes on a six month contract.
bullets: Work on a rare mass timber project using leading sustainable methods.
Help deliver a landmark regenerative building in Western Australia.
Hands-on, site-based role in a small team.
screening_questions: Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
Do you hold a Construction Induction Safety certificate (White Card)?
Do you have a current Australian driver's licence?
How many years' experience do you have as a site engineer?
candidates.content_text:
About us
We are a purpose-led construction company dedicated to delivering a landmark regenerative building in Western Australia.
Designed to set a new benchmark for sustainable construction, the project brings together low-carbon materials, renewable energy, and water-sensitive design to create a building that gives back more than it takes.
We work closely with the local community, industry partners, and specialist practitioners, and we share what we learn so others can build better too.
About the role
We are looking for a Site Engineer to join us on an initial 6 month, fixed term contract, with the possibility of extension.
You will provide site-based technical and coordination support to our Construction Manager, Project Manager, and wider project team. Your focus will be on reviewing drawings, finding design errors and discrepancies before they reach construction, coordinating trades, and verifying quality on site.
This role is based on site full time and involves daily site inspections.
We know good people work in different ways and we are open to discussing working arrangements that suit you, including hours, location, and how the week is structured. If there is an arrangement that would work better for you, we are happy to talk it through.
What you will do
- Review construction drawings at each revision, checking dimensions, setouts, levels, and cross-references between architectural, structural, and services documentation.
- Identify discrepancies, clashes, missing details, and buildability issues before work starts, and communicate changes between revisions to the trades they affect.
- Verify shop drawings against design drawings, take part in clash detection and building information modelling (BIM) reviews, and keep a drawing issue register through to closure.
- Keep trade interfaces, sequencing, and deliveries running smoothly with the Site Manager, including access, setout, service penetrations, embedments, and cast-in items.
- Make sure every trade works from current drawings, and escalate any works at risk of proceeding on incorrect or outdated information.
- Confirm setout, dimensions, and quality match the drawings before and during works, through inspection and test plans, hold point and witness inspections, pre-pour checks, and frame checks.
- Collect and verify site records, including moisture readings, cutting and penetration registers, survey checks, material dockets, and test certificates, and track non-conformances and defects through to closure.
- Draft and manage requests for information (RFIs) through to response, with supporting photos, markups, and measurements, and record site instructions and variations arising from design errors, including time and cost impacts.
About you
- Minimum of 5 years' site-based experience on commercial construction projects.
- Demonstrated ability to read and interrogate architectural, structural, and services drawings, with a track record of catching errors before construction.
- Strong setout and dimensional literacy, including levels, grids, and tolerances.
- Experience drafting RFIs and drawing markups.
- Working knowledge of Aconex or an equivalent platform.
- Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with all stakeholders.
- Sound judgement and initiative, with the ability to anticipate issues, resolve them independently, and escalate appropriately.
- Must hold a current White Card and WA driver's licence.
- High attention to detail, a collaborative approach, and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
- Experience on mass timber, structural steel, high specification and exposed services-dense projects is preferred.
- Trade experience or a tertiary qualification in construction management or engineering is preferred but not essential.
- Experience with BIM model review, such as Navisworks, is preferred but not essential.
- Familiarity with AS 3600, AS 3610, or structural tolerance standards is preferred but not essential.
We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences. If you do not tick every box but think you would be great in this role, we would still like to hear from you. We are committed to a fair and accessible recruitment process, please let us know if you need any adjustments to take part.
candidates.teaser: We are seeking a detail driven Site Engineer to lead quality through to finishes on a six month contract.

candidates.content_text:
Infrastructure Engineer
- $125k base + super + 5 weeks leave
- Kenmore office, free parking onsite, 2 days WFH. 
- Collaborative & autonomous team, wide range of projects.
About this role
At Churches of Christ, technology plays a critical role in supporting the services we deliver to communities across Queensland.
Our Infrastructure Engineer enjoys taking ownership, solving complex problems, and improving how technology supports the business. You will work across a broad enterprise environment spanning Azure, Microsoft 365, Active Directory, security, monitoring, SaaS platforms, databases, and business-critical applications.
You will be involved throughout the full solution lifecycle, from design and implementation through to optimisation and ongoing support. Working across both modern cloud platforms and legacy environments, you will help strengthen our security posture, improve operational resilience, and contribute to key infrastructure modernisation initiatives.
You will:
- Design, implement and support infrastructure solutions across Azure and Microsoft 365.
- Take ownership of core infrastructure platforms and services.
- Strengthen security, governance, monitoring, and operational resilience across the environment.
- Identify opportunities to automate manual processes and improve efficiency through scripting and automation.
- Support cloud migrations, platform upgrades, and infrastructure modernisation projects.
- Partner with application, technology, and business teams to deliver reliable, secure, and scalable solutions.
- Consider both technical and business impacts when making infrastructure decisions.
About you
You are a hands-on infrastructure professional who enjoys building, improving, and owning solutions rather than simply maintaining them. We are looking for experience across the following areas:
- Azure infrastructure and cloud services
- Microsoft 365 and SaaS platforms
- Active Directory and hybrid identity environments
- Infrastructure monitoring and operational support
- Security, governance, and compliance practices
- SIEM or security monitoring solutions
- SQL Server and supporting database infrastructure
- Infrastructure scripting and automation using PowerShell, SQL, or similar technologies.
- Infrastructure upgrades, migrations, and legacy system modernisation
Essential for the role.
Child Safety is everyone’s responsibility. Our robust screening and recruitment processes help ensure we engage the right people to support children and young people. This role will require the following to be obtained before commencing:
- Possess a National Police Check,
- Working with Children (Blue Card),
- Licensed Care Service (Child Protection) or the ability to acquire.
Who we are – Churches of Christ 
Churches of Christ is one of Australia’s largest and most diverse not-for-profit organisations, delivering a range of care and community services across Residential Aged Care, Home Care and Retirement Living, Foster and Kinship Care and, Housing Support for over 140 years.  
We are guided by our values of Integrity, Compassion, Excellence and Courage, and we welcome everyone, of all backgrounds and faiths, as we foster a diverse and inclusive community for our people.
Why Join Our Team  
- Transformative leadership and a high performing team culture.  
- Opportunities for career development, stretch assignments and progression.  
- A growing national not-for-profit organisation with purpose and community impact.  
- Work in an inclusive, down to earth & welcoming culture.  
- 5 weeks annual leave  
- Hybrid / flexible working arrangements to support your work life balance. 
- Free on-site parking + on-site café with staff discount (at the Kenmore head office).  
- Not for profit salary packaging up to $18,549 which could be used for up to $15,900 (for everyday living expenses like rent, mortgage, school fees and many more) and up to $2,650 for meals and entertainment.

How many years of estimating experience do you have?
candidates.content_text:
About the role
We are seeking a highly experienced Estimator with a strong background in commercial ceilings and partitions, ideally with additional experience estimating carpentry and fit-out packages. This is a full-time, office-based position suited to someone who understands the industry, can read and interpret construction drawings confidently, and is capable of independently preparing accurate, competitive tenders.
Key responsibilities
- Prepare detailed estimates and tenders for commercial ceilings, partitions and carpentry packages.
- Complete accurate material and labour take-offs from construction drawings.
- Review architectural drawings, specifications and tender documentation.
- Identify scope gaps, discrepancies, exclusions and potential variations.
- Obtain and assess supplier and subcontractor quotations.
- Prepare competitive pricing submissions and tender breakdowns.
- Liaise with builders, suppliers, subcontractors and our internal project team.
- Assist with project handovers and procurement where required.
- Manage multiple tenders and meet submission deadlines.
About you

candidates.content_text:
Build Your Future Career with NEX Building Group
At Wilson Homes, we’re proud to call Tasmania home. For more than three decades, we’ve been the state’s leading new home builder, and we still get excited seeing families walk into their brand‑new homes for the first time. Safety, innovation and quality guide everything we do, and we’re always looking for new ways to improve, grow and support the people who make our work possible.
We are part of the NEX Building Group, an Australian network of more than 1300 passionate people who all share one purpose: to build beautiful homes for Australians
We are excited to offer Graduate opportunities within our 2027 Graduate Program, providing you with the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals, develop technical and leadership capabilities, and build a successful long-term career within our growing organisation. This opportunity is ideally suited to graduates with a passion for residential construction, drafting and estimating.
About the Program
Commencing February 2027, our structured 2-year Graduate Program provides exposure to multiple areas of the residential building industry through a series of rotations. You’ll be based in the office Monday to Friday.
Throughout the program, graduates will participate in:
•Soft skills and professional development workshops
•Keynote speaker sessions with industry and business leaders
•A collaborative graduate group project
•Leadership development opportunities
•Tours of Supaloc, MyChoice, display homes and key supplier locations
•Dedicated mentor and buddy support
Following successful completion of the program, graduates will transition into a permanent role within NEX Building Group.
About You
We're looking for enthusiastic graduates who:
•Graduated in 2025 or 2026
•Hold a degree in Construction Management, Building and design, Built Environment, Property Development, Project Management, Trade Qualification or related discipline. 
•Have strong communication and relationship-building skills
•Demonstrate initiative, curiosity and a willingness to learn
•Are passionate about building a long-term career in the residential construction industry
•Are willing to undertake occasional interstate travel as part of the Graduate Program
Why Join NEX Building Group?
At NEX Building Group, our people are at the centre of everything we do. We foster a collaborative, inclusive and innovative culture where graduates are empowered to contribute from day one.
You'll benefit from:
•A structured career development pathway
•Exposure to multiple areas of the business
•Senior leader mentoring and support
•Strong networking opportunities across our brands
•Ongoing learning and development programs
•A clear transition into a permanent role at the completion of the program
•Employee benefits: Discounts on gym membership, motor vehicle, health insurance and MORE!
What You'll Need to Apply
We want your application journey to be as smooth as possible, so here's what you'll need to prepare:
•Your CV and Academic Transcripts
•A Cover Letter: Tell us about yourself, why are you interested, your career aspirations and where you'd like to grow within the business.
Interested?
The appointment of successful applicants will be subject to satisfactory employment screening and, depending on the inherent requirements of the role, may involve the completion of a National Police Check and pre-employment medical.
Applications are now open, with offers expected to be extended by the end of November 2026.
If you are determined to build a long-term career and want to join an innovative and inclusive organisation committed to building better lives, click Apply Now.
To find out more about NEX Building Group, visit www.nexbg.com.au, follow us on LinkedIn, or contact our Talent Acquisition Team at careers@nexbg.com.au.
If you're ready to build your future with one of Australia's leading residential building groups, apply now and join our 2027 Graduate Program.

candidates.content_text:
Design the systems that keep people safe.
Every building needs fire protection and every system starts on a drawing. As a Designer / Draftsperson in our Fire Protection team, you’ll turn briefs into the technical documentation that gets fire protection systems built on real projects across Melbourne — and you’ll be able to point to the buildings you helped protect.
You don’t need to have worked in fire protection before. If you’re confident in Revit and AutoCAD and have a sharp eye for detail, we’ll teach you the fire protection side.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
•     Meet with clients, builders and other trades to understand project briefs
•     Create, review, mark up and produce technical design documentation
•     Visit sites to check conditions and keep drawings accurate and current
•     Deliver your work to specifications, budgets and timelines
WHAT YOU’LL GET
•     Hands-on training in fire protection design and the relevant Australian Standards
•     A clear career pathway with an established company that has led the construction industry for over 40 years
•     Diverse work across a wide range of projects, with a collaborative team that backs you up
•     Hybrid/flexible working arrangements
•     Office is close to public transport
•     Competitive salary
•     Awesome company culture and cohesive team
•     Monthly morning teas and team meets
•     6 wellbeing days a year on us
WHAT YOU’LL BRING
•     Proficiency in Revit and AutoCAD (essential)
•     Drafting or design experience (architectural, civil, mechanical, building design or similar) — fire protection experience not required
•     A sharp eye for detail and accuracy, and the ability to stay calm when deadlines tighten
•     Clear written and verbal communication, and a team-first attitude
•     A current driver’s licence
WHO WE WANT TO HEAR FROM
We welcome career changers, recent graduates, people returning to work, women, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, and people from all backgrounds. If you meet most of the above but not all of it, we’d still like to hear from you.
Applicants must be Australian citizens or permanent residents, or hold a valid Australian work visa. Successful applicants will complete pre-employment checks, including a National Police Check.

candidates.content_text:
The Opportunity:
Maitland City Council's Pathways program is a fantastic way to kick-start your career and gain professional experience in local government!
Commencing in January 2027, for a period of two years, we have two exciting opportunities for Graduate Civil Engineers to join our organisation.
In this role, you will undertake a graduate program developed specifically for you, giving you exposure to a range of civil engineering functions for the investigation and delivery of civil and recreation infrastructure projects undertaken by Council. These duties are going to help you develop a solid foundation to your civil engineering career.
About you:
To be successful in this role you will possess:
- Degree level qualifications in Civil engineering in the previous two years or completion of degree by January 2027
- Contemporary industry knowledge of civil engineering areas
- Experience and understanding in project support and the research, analysis and presentation of information
- Current Class C driver's licence
Benefits:
This Graduate position is temporary full time (two-year contract) with a commencing salary of $1,414.58 weekly, plus 12% superannuation. Graduates will also have access to Council's great staff benefits including:
- Flexible work arrangements
- One extra week of "My Leave" a year (to use how you like!)
- Ongoing training and development
- Fitness Passport
- Healthy Employee Program
To apply:
To apply for this opportunity, please click 'Apply Now' and submit your resume and cover letter.
Questions:
To viw the role charter click 'Apply Now'. If after reading the role charter you have any questions, please contact the recruitment team at Recruitment@maitland.nsw.gov.au
More information regarding Council's Pathways Program can be viewed via https://www.maitland.nsw.gov.au/pathways-program.
Applications close: Sunday 25th October 2027
Only candidates with current Australian work rights (Australian citizens, permanent residents, NZ citizens with a current passport, valid work visa) will be considered.
What happens next?
Once applications close, we will review all candidates' details against the role requirements and will be back in touch with you to advise the status of your application.
Please note, prior to an offer of employment being made, recommended candidates will be required to undertake a medical assessment (including drug and alcohol testing). Council also completes a range of other pre-employment checks which may include reference checks, psychometric testing or a criminal history check. For more information about the recruitment process, visit the "Jobs at Council" page on our website.

Maitland City Council is dedicated to providing a workplace that is inclusive and supportive and is reflective of the diverse community we serve. We support equal opportunities for all employees, and encourage applications from people from all cultures, nationalities, identities, and abilities. We believe all employees have the right to feel valued, respected and heard. If you have any special considerations or accessibility requirements, please let us know in the recruitment process how we are able to meet your needs.
 If you require special assistance, or have any questions about the recruitment process please contact us for a confidential conversation (Recruitment@maitland.nsw.gov.au)

candidates.content_text:
Build your career with an organisation that is invested in your success. 
Maker Consulting Services is looking for a motivated Civil Engineering Undergraduate or Graduate to join our growing Newcastle team. Whether you're currently studying and looking to gain meaningful industry experience alongside university; or completing your degree and ready to begin your graduate career, this role offers the opportunity to develop your technical skills while contributing to real projects from day one. 
You'll work alongside experienced engineers on land development, infrastructure, roads and stormwater projects across Newcastle, the Hunter and broader NSW, gaining practical experience that complements your university studies and builds the foundation for your professional career. 
At Maker, we believe in providing a flexible work lifestyle. This has inspired us to change the way we work, leaving behind the traditional 5-day work week. Instead, Maker has adopted a 4-day work week, providing you with a day off during the week and giving you the time to catch up on life and do more of what you love!  
For undergraduate candidates, we offer flexibility around university timetables and exam periods, allowing you to gain consistent industry experience while completing your degree. 
Why join Maker 
Maker is a fast-growing, multi-disciplinary consultancy with more than 65 employees across 4 offices in NSW and Victoria. In addition to Civil Engineering, we specialise in Town Planning, Surveying, and Project Management which provides you with the opportunity to collaborate across a wide range of exciting projects. 
You’ll enjoy:
- Hands-on mentoring from experienced civil engineers, including direct exposure to senior members of our Newcastle team.  
- Real project involvement from the outset - not just observation or administrative tasks.  
- Experience across land development, roads, stormwater, infrastructure and multidisciplinary projects.  
- Opportunities to develop your skills in industry-standard civil design and modelling software.  
- A supportive culture where questions are encouraged and knowledge is shared. 
- The opportunity to grow from undergraduate engineer through to graduate and increasingly independent project responsibilities.  
- A 4-day working week, giving you more time to enjoy life outside work 
- Modern offices and regular team social events 
About the Role 
Located in our Newcastle office and working closely with our Newcastle Principal Civil Engineer, you will be exposed to a variety of projects that will introduce you to a broad range of civil engineering disciplines and progressively build your technical and professional capability. 
Your responsibilities will include: 
- Assisting with the design and documentation of civil infrastructure and land development projects, including roads, earthworks, stormwater drainage and utility infrastructure. 
- Developing practical experience using industry-standard civil design and modelling software. 
- Assisting with engineering calculations, technical assessments and preparation of reports. 
- Working with engineers, surveyors, planners and project managers to understand how projects progress from concept through to construction. 
- Participating in site inspections, project meetings and coordination activities where appropriate. 
You'll be encouraged to ask questions, learn from experienced professionals and progressively take on greater responsibility as your confidence grows. 
For undergraduate candidates, our aim is to provide meaningful, ongoing employment throughout your studies, with flexible part-time arrangements to suit university commitments and the opportunity to transition into a graduate position as you complete your degree. 
About You 
We're looking for someone curious, motivated and excited to build a career in Civil Engineering. 
We're looking for:
- Someone currently studying a Bachelor's degree in Civil or Environmental Engineering, or who has recently graduated from a relevant engineering degree. 
- A genuine interest in civil engineering and a willingness to learn. 
- An interest in design, problem-solving and seeing projects progress from concept through to construction. 
- Good written and verbal communication skills, with an interest in developing your technical writing capability. 
- Good time management, organisation and prioritisation skills. 
- The ability to work both independently and as part of a collaborative team. 
Whether you're part-way through your degree and looking to build industry experience alongside your studies, or approaching graduation and ready to begin your professional career, we'd like to hear from you. 
Ready to Build Your Career? 
If you're looking to gain meaningful civil engineering experience while completing your degree, or you're ready to take the first step in your graduate career, we'd love to hear from you. 
Please submit your resume and a short cover letter telling us a little about yourself, your studies and why you're interested in joining Maker by clicking the APPLY button.

candidates.content_text:
The Opportunity
Our client who is a first class civil engineering consultancy who is seeking a Graduate Civil Engineer to join their experienced Cairns-based engineering team.
This is an opportunity to apply your technical skills to projects that have a genuine impact, from roads that connect communities and drainage systems that protect property, through to bridges, culverts, water infrastructure and land development projects.
This consultancy provides civil engineering and project management services across government, private development, infrastructure and regional projects throughout Far North Queensland and beyond. Their project portfolio includes roads and drainage, water and wastewater infrastructure, subdivisions, bridge and crossing works, airports and major infrastructure projects.
The Role
You will be a hands-on member of the engineering team, contributing to the planning, design and delivery of a broad range of civil infrastructure projects.
This is more than producing drawings and technical reports. You will see projects progress from concept and design through to construction and completion, working alongside experienced engineers, clients, contractors and other stakeholders.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Developing practical and cost-effective civil infrastructure designs
- Supporting road, drainage, stormwater, water and land development projects
- Preparing technical drawings, documentation and engineering reports
- Assisting with project delivery and undertaking site inspections
- Monitoring construction outcomes, quality and project requirements
- Identifying technical issues and developing practical solutions
- Supporting approvals, compliance and stakeholder requirements
- Liaising professionally with clients, contractors and project stakeholders
- Working closely with senior engineers while developing your technical capability
About You
You will be a motivated Civil Engineer who enjoys civil design, practical problem solving and wants exposure to a diverse range of projects.
You will ideally have:
- Degree qualification in Civil Engineering
- Practical experience in civil design is a must
- Exposure to roads, drainage, stormwater, water, subdivisions or similar projects
- Strong technical and problem-solving skills
- Good attention to detail and an ability to manage competing priorities
- Clear written and verbal communication skills
- A practical approach to engineering and project delivery
- Current driver's licence and willingness to attend project sites
This role could suit an early-career Civil Engineer looking to build broader consulting experience, or an Engineer with several years of experience seeking greater project variety and responsibility.
Why Join This Engineering Consultancy?
They offer the opportunity to work alongside experienced Civil Engineers and project professionals on projects across both metropolitan and regional environments. The business places a strong emphasis on professional development, practical experience, integrity and delivering quality outcomes for its clients.
Job Offer
- $75,000 - $85,000 + super, negotiable based on experience
- Relocation assistance available
- Diverse civil projects from concept and design through to construction
- Exposure to roads, drainage, water, infrastructure and land development
- Hands-on project and site experience
- Mentoring from experienced senior engineers
- Ongoing training and professional development
- Opportunity to contribute ideas and influence project outcomes
- Supportive and collaborative team environment
- Long-term career stability and genuine project variety
How To Apply
To build your career with a company that values quality engineering, practical solutions and the work you deliver, please click Apply and please include any civil design experience you have undertaken in your application.
About Us
With Head Office in Cairns and offices in Townsville and Brisbane. We specialise in professional, administration, engineering and industrial recruitment, permanent and temporary placements for both commercial and government enterprise. We are proud to connect great people with meaningful careers.

candidates.salary: Includes iPhone, Laptop and other benefits
bullets: Global mobility opportunities through being part of VINCI
Leadership development programs & one on one mentoring

candidates.content_text:
Build More. Build Your Career.
Ready to kick-start your engineering career on some of Southeast Queensland’s most exciting infrastructure projects?
Seymour Whyte's Graduate Program gives ambitious engineering graduates the opportunity to work on major projects, take on real responsibility from day one, and develop the technical, commercial and leadership skills needed for a successful career in construction.
Through our structured two-year development program, you'll gain hands-on experience across major civil infrastructure projects, work alongside industry leaders, receive dedicated mentoring and build the skills and confidence to accelerate your career.  You'll be trusted with real responsibility, supported to grow and given the opportunity to make a genuine impact while helping deliver infrastructure that connects communities.
About the Project
We have an exciting opportunity for a Graduate Civil Engineer to join our Beerburrum to Nambour (B2N) Rail Upgrade project.
This a major infrastructure project transforming the North Coast Line on the Sunshine Coast. The project includes rail duplication, new and upgraded transport infrastructure, improved road overpasses and enhanced signalling systems, all aimed at increasing capacity and reliability across the network. Once complete, B2N will deliver faster and more efficient travel while improving connections between the Sunshine Coast, Moreton Bay and Brisbane, creating lasting benefits for local communities and the region.
Why Join Seymour Whyte?
At Seymour Whyte, we believe the best way to learn is by doing. Our structured Graduate Development Program is designed to fast-track your career through hands-on project experience, mentoring from industry leaders and tailored professional development opportunities.
From day one, you'll be embedded in a live project team, contributing to the delivery of major infrastructure projects that shape communities across Australia. You'll gain exposure to a range of disciplines, build your technical and commercial acumen and develop the confidence to take ownership of meaningful work early in your career.
Throughout the program, you'll be supported by experienced mentors, participate in structured development workshops, and connect with a national network of graduates and professionals who are invested in your success.
What's in it for you?
- Work on a landmark civil infrastructure project from day one
- Gain exposure to multiple disciplines across project delivery
- Receive structured mentoring, coaching and development support
- Learn from experienced industry leaders and subject matter experts
- Build a strong professional network across projects and regions
- Be part of a collaborative, supportive and high-performing team culture
- Access career opportunities within the VINCI Group, a global leader in construction, infrastructure and concessions
Whether your passion lies in construction delivery, engineering, project management or leadership, our Graduate Development Program will provide the foundation, support and opportunities to help you build a rewarding and long-term career with Seymour Whyte.
To learn more about our Graduate Program, click here.
About You
You're in your final year of a Bachelor of Civil Engineering and ready to turn everything you've learned into real-world experience on major infrastructure projects.
Whether you've gained experience through an internship, vacation work, industry placement or part-time employment, you're eager to learn, build your skills and make a meaningful contribution from day one.
We're looking for graduates who are curious, motivated and excited about a career in civil construction.
You'll bring:
- Final-year studies in a Bachelor of Civil Engineering
- Practical experience through internships, vacation programs, placements or other employment
- A genuine passion for civil construction and infrastructure projects
- A positive attitude and willingness to learn from experienced industry professionals
- Strong communication and teamwork skills
- A commitment to safety, collaboration and creating a positive team culture
- Flexibility to travel or relocate as opportunities arise throughout your career
Most importantly, you're ready to take the next step, embrace new challenges and build a rewarding career delivering projects that make a lasting impact on communities across Australia.
Seymour Whyte Benefits
- Employee recognition and awards that celebrate contribution and achievement
- An employee share program, providing the opportunity to invest in the long-term success of the business
- Birthday leave, because celebrating life's milestones matters
- The option to purchase additional leave to support travel, study or personal commitments
- Fitness and wellbeing discounts through WHEREFIT (gym memberships, meal plans and fitness brands)
- Travel, retail, lifestyle and wellness discounts
- Workplace banking benefits and everyday financial savings through CommBank and Flare
Seymour Whyte is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and we encourage applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds, including veterans.
Our commitment to an equitable construction industry extends to an inclusive culture that embraces our differences and gives everyone the opportunity to grow and be equally valued. We're unified in our direction toward having a workplace that is balanced and fair for all.
Next Steps:
- Submit your CV online to apply for this role
- All successful applicants will be required to undergo a pre-employment medical and criminal history check
- Applications will only be accepted from candidates who have the right to work in Australia
To learn more about us, visit www.seymourwhyte.com.au

candidates.abstract: Join GPA Engineering as a Civil/Structural Drafter. Work on diverse industrial projects and further develop your 2D drafting and 3D modelling skills.
bullets: Great company culture and supportive team environment
Structured career progression pathway and company-sponsored training
Broaden your technical capability, work across a diverse range of projects

What motivated you to apply for this position?

If you are on a Visa, please indicate your Visa number (eg. 190, 485) and the expiry date.

We are committed to providing an inclusive recruitment process. If you require any adjustments to help you participate fully (e.g. different interview format, accessible location, extra time), please indicate below (optional):
candidates.content_text:
About Us
For over 35 years, GPA Engineering has been a trusted, Australian-owned consultancy delivering engineering, procurement and construction management services across water, energy, renewables, defence, mining, and hydrogen. We develop and implement projects that drive critical infrastructure and support industries across Australia.
With offices nationwide (Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne, Sydney, Darwin, Perth) and a reputation for technical excellence, our strength lies in our people. We bring together diverse, motivated professionals who value teamwork, integrity, safety, and sustainability. At GPA, you’ll find the scale and expertise of a leading consultancy, combined with the supportive culture of a close-knit team.
About the Role
With a strong pipeline of projects across the energy, resources and industrial sectors, GPA Engineering is seeking an experienced Civil/Structural Drafter to join our Adelaide team.
Based in our Adelaide Head Office, you will work as part of a multidisciplinary team delivering projects across oil & gas, mining, materials handling, water and power. This role is suited to someone with 3-10 years' experience who enjoys variety, technical challenges and developing high-quality 2D drawings and 3D models.
Working closely with engineers and designers, you'll contribute to projects from concept through to detailed design, gaining exposure to a broad range of clients and industries. You'll have the opportunity to further develop your drafting and modelling skills while taking increasing ownership of design documentation and model coordination.
Key Duties:
 - Prepare, revise and maintain civil and structural engineering drawings and 3D models across a range of projects.
 - Produce high-quality 2D deliverables including general arrangements, plans, elevations, sections and construction details.
 - Develop and maintain 3D models to support coordinated multidisciplinary project delivery.
 - Work closely with engineers and designers to translate engineering concepts and calculations into clear and practical design documentation.
 - Apply relevant Australian Standards, client specifications, project requirements and GPA drafting standards.
 - Participate in drawing and model reviews and incorporate design changes and review comments.
 - Coordinate with other engineering disciplines to identify and resolve design interfaces and clashes.
 - Manage assigned drafting activities to meet project schedules and agreed deliverables.
 - Ensure drawings, models and associated documentation comply with GPA quality assurance requirements
We are looking for a collaborative and technically capable Civil/Structural Drafter with strong attention to detail and a practical approach to engineering documentation.
The successful candidate will ideally have:
 - Qualifications: An Associate Degree in Civil and Structural Engineering (Design Drafting), Advanced Diploma or equivalent recognised drafting/design qualification, either completed or currently being undertaken.
 - Experience: Approximately 3–10 years of relevant civil and/or structural drafting and design experience earthworks.
 - Industry Experience: Experience in heavy industry sectors such as oil & gas, mining, materials handling, water or power will be highly regarded.
 - 2D Drafting: Strong capability in producing engineering drawings including general arrangements, plans, elevations, sections and construction details.
 - 3D Modelling: Experience developing and working with 3D models as part of coordinated engineering project delivery.
 - Software: Proficiency in AutoCAD and/or MicroStation. Experience with Civil 3D, Advance Steel, Revit or other relevant design and modelling software would be advantageous.
 - Technical Understanding: Ability to interpret engineering mark-ups, design information, relevant Australian Standards and client specifications.
 - Quality: Strong attention to detail and an understanding of engineering drawing standards, document control and QA processes.
 - Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively both independently and within multidisciplinary project teams.
A requirement for this role is to complete a satisfactory pre-employment medical check and Australian police clearance. 
At GPA, we want our people to thrive both professionally and personally. We’re big enough to deliver complex, high-profile projects, yet small enough that you’ll be known, valued and supported.
 - Competitive Salary & Rewards – an attractive remuneration package, including paid overtime, recognising the value of the work you put in.
 - Career Growth & Development – structured career progression, company-sponsored training, mentoring and support towards professional membership and Chartership.
 - Diverse Project Exposure – opportunities to work across different industries, clients and project types, building broad technical and practical experience.
 - Flexibility – hybrid working options and cultural leave swap days, supporting a healthy balance between work and life.
 - Health & Wellbeing – wellbeing programs, confidential EAP support and a workplace culture that looks out for its people.
 - Family-Friendly Benefits – paid parental leave for primary and secondary carers, together with policies designed to support different stages of life.
 - Community & Culture – opportunities to connect beyond project work through sporting and fitness groups, social events, family BBQs, quiz nights and celebrations of diverse cultural traditions.
 - Giving Back – a strong commitment to the community, with GPA having donated more than $3 million directly to charitable organisations.
 - Diversity & Inclusion – a workplace where different perspectives are respected and collaboration is encouraged.
At GPA, we offer a supportive working environment where people can build long-term careers. More than 80 of our team members have been with GPA for over 10 years, reflecting the opportunities, culture and stability we aim to provide.
Hear from our people and learn more about working at GPA through our Careers page (https://www.gpaeng.com.au/careers/).
GPA is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences.
How to Apply
Submit your applications through our online recruitment system before EOD 30th October 2026.
If you require adjustments to the recruitment process to support your application, you may email us at HR@gpaeng.com.au.
Disclaimer to Recruitment Agencies: 
Please be advised that GPA Engineering does not accept resumes submitted by third-party recruitment agencies. All job applications must be submitted directly by the candidate through our official career portal or via direct contact with our HR team. We will not be held liable for any fees or claims from recruitment agencies regarding unsolicited resumes or candidate submissions. We appreciate your understanding and cooperation.

candidates.title: Project Planning Engineer – Civil Infrastructure
candidates.abstract: Shape a growing City’s infrastructure. Plan capital projects through design, costing and approvals, with WFH and flexi-time for a 9-day fortnight.
bullets: Shape civil infrastructure projects across asset renewal, upgrades and growth.
Flexible working with WFH and accrued flexi-time towards a 9-day fortnight.
$102,000–$117,000 + super up to 15%, subject to conditions + free gym membership
candidates.content_text:
City of Armadale
Armadale, Perth WA
Engineering – Civil/Structural Engineering 
$102,000–$117,000 per annum plus superannuation
Shape a growing City’s infrastructure. Plan capital projects through design, costing and approvals, with WFH and flexi-time for a 9-day fortnight.
 -  Shape infrastructure projects across asset renewal, upgrades and growth.
 -  Flexible working with WFH and accrued flexi-time towards a 9-day fortnight.
 -  Superannuation up to 15%, subject to conditions, plus free gym membership.
 Help shape the projects that shape our City
Good infrastructure starts with good decisions. Understanding what is needed, testing the options and resolving the detail before construction begins.
At the City of Armadale, you’ll help make those decisions. As one of Western Australia’s fastest-growing local governments, we’re planning new infrastructure while improving and renewing the assets our community already relies on.
We’re looking for a Project Planning Engineer who brings practical judgement, asks good questions and takes pride in preparing projects properly.
If you’re enjoying your current role but would welcome the opportunity to influence a growing City’s infrastructure, this could be your next move.
Why Armadale?
Our Strategic Community Plan sets a clear direction: facilities that meet community needs, better public places, and infrastructure that is functional, inclusive and sustainable.
You’ll help turn those priorities into practical projects, balancing technical requirements, cost, risk and long-term asset performance. Across renewal, upgrade and growth projects, you’ll tackle varied challenges and see how your work contributes to the community.
You’ll also have flexibility in how you work, including working from home and the ability to accrue flexi-time to work a nine-day fortnight, with arrangements agreed around role and team requirements.
Your role
Working in our Asset Planning team, reporting to the Project Planning Lead, you’ll progress identified infrastructure priorities into well-defined, costed and approved capital projects ready for delivery.
Starting with Project Initiation Documents developed by Strategic Asset Management, you’ll coordinate investigations and detailed designs, refine cost estimates and progress the approvals needed for capital works program entry.
You’ll work with engineering and landscape design specialists, consultants, asset operators and delivery teams to:
 - Develop clear project scopes, specifications and budget requirements.
 - Coordinate investigations, technical advice and detailed design activities.
 - Prepare and refine cost estimates, checking assumptions, contingencies and constructability.
 - Progress approvals, utility clearances, statutory consents and other project requirements.
 - Prepare complete project packages for review under the City’s Project Management Framework.
 - Resolve risks and gaps early, considering procurement, construction sequencing and handover requirements.
Your work will help the City make informed investment decisions and give delivery teams confidence in each project’s scope, cost and readiness.
What you’ll bring
You know what it takes to prepare an infrastructure project for delivery. You can work through technical detail, challenge assumptions constructively and bring the right people together to resolve issues.
We’re looking for:
 - Tertiary qualifications in Civil Engineering, Project Management, Construction Management or a closely related discipline**, or equivalent demonstrated experience in project planning and infrastructure development.
 - Experience planning civil infrastructure or construction projects.
 - Sound knowledge of cost estimation, contingency allowances and key cost drivers.
 - The ability to coordinate technical input across disciplines and progress third-party approvals.
 - Familiarity with project management frameworks and project approval requirements.
Flexibility and benefits
 - Working-from-home arrangements and flexi-time, including the ability to accrue time towards a nine-day fortnight.
 - Superannuation contributions of up to 15%, subject to employee contributions and applicable conditions.
 - Free Armadale Fitness and Aquatic Centre membership**, including the gym, pools, sauna and group fitness classes.
 - Wellbeing activities throughout the year.
 - Novated leasing opportunities.
Our values—Care; Are Better, Together; Learn & Grow; and Seize Today, Shape Tomorrow—guide how we work. We listen, share knowledge and welcome people who bring ideas and take responsibility for their work.
Interested? Let’s talk
You don’t need to be actively looking for a new job to explore this opportunity.
For an initial confidential conversation, contact People Services on 9394 5189 or hr@armadale.wa.gov.au. 
Ready to apply? Submit your CV and a brief cover letter through the application link, outlining your relevant experience and interest in the role.
We review applications as they are received and may close the advertisement early.
*The City of Armadale welcomes applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability, people from culturally diverse backgrounds and people of all genders and identities.*
*We are committed to child safety and recruitment practices that support a safe and inclusive community.*

candidates.content_text:
Civil Draftsperson (MicroStation & ProjectWise)
Join Hullcon
At Hullcon, we believe in Design with Delivery in Mind. Our work is practical, buildable and shaped by real delivery experience across transport infrastructure, renewables and civil engineering projects. We work closely with clients, contractors and delivery partners to develop solutions that perform both on paper and in the field.
We're looking for an experienced Civil Draftsperson who is highly proficient in Bentley MicroStation and ProjectWise and is excited about contributing to major infrastructure and renewable energy projects across Australia.
This is an office-based role in our Abbotsford office, designed to maximise collaboration with our engineers, designers and project managers.
The Role
You will be responsible for the preparation, management and coordination of high-quality engineering drawings and models for civil infrastructure projects. You will also be responsible for administering our ProjectWise system.
Working alongside experienced engineers and design managers, you'll play a key role in delivering documentation across a diverse portfolio that includes:
- Roads and highways
- Civil infrastructure
- Renewable energy projects
- Drainage and earthworks
- Buildings and associated civil works
- Temporary and permanent works
You will also have the opportunity to broaden your skillset into structural drafting and help drive the adoption of AI-enabled drafting workflows and automation tools.
What You'll Be Doing
- Producing civil and structural engineering drawings using Bentley MicroStation
- Managing project documentation and workflows in ProjectWise
- Coordinating drawing production across multidisciplinary teams
- Assisting with document control and drawing management
- Leading CAD standards, drafting efficiency and quality processes
- Exploring and implementing AI tools to improve drafting productivity, consistency and quality
- Structural drafting where required
About You
We're looking for someone who has:
Essential
- Strong experience using Bentley MicroStation and/or OpenRoads Designer
- Strong experience using and managing ProjectWise
- Experience drafting civil infrastructure projects in Victoria, particularly on major projects
- Excellent attention to detail and drawing presentation
- Strong understanding of engineering documentation standards
- Ability to work collaboratively within a project team
- Strong communication and organisational skills
Desirable
- Experience with OpenRoads Designer
- Experience with renewable energy projects
- Structural drafting experience
- Interest in automation, digital engineering and AI tools
- Experience working in ISO-aligned quality environments
- Experience in training and managing other drafters
Why Join Hullcon?
- Work directly with senior engineers and project leaders
- Exposure to major transport and renewable energy projects
- Genuine opportunity to shape how AI is used within engineering design

Competitive salary package
Contribute to a sustainable and greener future.
candidates.content_text:
ACCIONA is a global company, leading in the development of regenerative infrastructure that creates a positive impact on society. Our workforce consists of more than 65,000 professionals, present in more than 40 countries across the five continents, all contributing to our mission to design a better planet. Are you a passionate individual who wants to make a difference, promote sustainable development, and find solutions to the biggest global challenges, including climate change, overpopulation, and water scarcity? Come and join us in building the infrastructure our planet needs to achieve a sustainable future.
ACEREZ, a partnership of ACCIONA, COBRA and Endeavour Energy, has been appointed network operator by EnergyCo to design, build, finance, operate and maintain the Central-West Orana Renewable Energy Zone (REZ) transmission network. The ACCIONA COBRA Joint Venture (ACJV), the design and construct (D&C) consortium, will design and build the Central-West Orana REZ transmission project.
The Central-West Orana Renewable Energy Zone (REZ) Transmission Project will build new high-capacity transmission lines, energy hubs and supporting infrastructure to transfer power generated by solar and wind projects to electricity consumers. The new infrastructure is expected to be operational by 2028 and will initially unlock up to 4.5 gigawatts of new network capacity.
The project consists of 90km of 500kV overhead transmission lines and 150 km of 330kV transmission lines for generator connections, stretching from Elong Elong in the west through to Barigan Creek in the east, via an energy hub at Merotherie.
The Central-West Orana project is currently seeking a dedicated Site Engineer - Civil to share their expertise within our growing Energy Hubs and Substations Teams.
Key Responsibilities
- Ensure all quality and environmental aspects of the project are addressed to maintain effective operation and project delivery.
- Ensures non-conformances are recorded and corrective actions initiated as soon as practically possible.
- Completes all outstanding defects as required by the program.
- Prepares Inspection Test Reports and checklists that accurately reflect contract requirements.
- Provide support on planning the use of materials, resources, components or systems within the project, and construction practices and problems to ensure project success, value for money and best practice are achieved.
- Assist the Project Engineer with development of construction planning documents and monitor implementation.
- Maintain project schedule by monitoring project progress and coordinating activities.
- Assist with preparing project status reports and change orders.
- Assesses progress daily and prepares plan of works for daily cost planning meeting (if held)
- Responsible and accountable to ensure that the requirements of the Contract are being satisfied at work crew level.
- Coordinate resource allocation with the expectation that you would encourage effective teamwork and foster a positive attitude toward the achievement of organisational objectives.
- Tracks subcontractor resources daily and record accurately
- Prepares cost plan/resources for daily cost planning meeting.
Required Skills and Competencies
- Bachelor's degree (Engineering) Civil or Relevant Tertiary Education
- Experience constructing outdoor air insulated substations and substations at 220kV or above
- Tier 1 Contractor experience is preferred, on large scale projects
- Preferable 1 to 3 years post graduate experience in a construction / engineering environment
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively with others.
- Establish and steward overall delivery work plans.
- Ensuring all relevant regulatory requirements are satisfied.
- Competent in planning and organising work schedules.
- Working knowledge of HS&E requirements and implementation of same
- Clear communication - verbal and written
Site Engineer positions are bus in bus out, in camp style accommodation provided for 14 days onsite and 7 days off site, on a roster-based arrangement out of the Central West Orana Region, Merotherie.
This position is being delivered as part of a joint venture between two organisations. As such, your employment may be with either of the parent companies, and this will be confirmed during the recruitment process.
We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. If you believe you bring the capabilities to succeed in this role, we'd love to hear from you. We look forward to continuing to build our supportive workplace together.
For more information on how your personal data is managed, please refer to the privacy statements of each parent company:
Grupo Cobra: https://www.grupocobra.com/en/privacy-policy/
Acciona: Privacy Policy | ACCIONA | Business as unusual

About the role
Duffy Kennedy Constructions (DKC) is seeking an experienced and motivated Civil Engineering Draftsperson to join our team in Miranda, NSW. This full-time position plays an important role in supporting our ongoing construction projects by preparing accurate technical drawings, coordinating design documentation, and providing timely drafting support to project managers and site teams. The successful candidate will work closely with our design and construction teams, contributing to the efficient delivery of residential, commercial and other building projects.
Key responsibilities
- Prepare and amend detailed civil and structural engineering drawings using AutoCAD, Revit or other relevant drafting software.
- Produce technical drawings for earthworks, drainage systems, foundations, reinforced concrete elements and other construction components.
- Interpret engineering calculations, design specifications and technical sketches to develop accurate construction drawings and documentation.
- Review and update drawings to reflect design changes, construction requirements and actual site conditions.
- Conduct site visits when required to verify construction details, identify discrepancies and assist with drawing revisions.
- Liaise with engineers, estimators, project managers and subcontractors to ensure drawings meet project requirements and relevant Australian Standards.
- Provide technical drafting support to construction teams and assist in resolving drawing-related issues during project execution.
- Maintain accurate drawing records, documentation and version control throughout the project lifecycle.
About you
- Relevant tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering, Engineering Drafting, Architectural Engineering or a related discipline.
- Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in civil or structural engineering drafting, preferably within the building construction industry.
- Proficiency in AutoCAD, Revit or similar drafting software.
- Sound understanding of civil and structural engineering principles, construction methods and technical drawing standards.
- Experience preparing detailed drawings for residential, commercial or multi-storey building projects will be highly regarded.
- Strong attention to detail, problem-solving abilities and organisational skills.
- Good communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with engineers, project managers and construction personnel.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks and respond efficiently to changing project requirements.
Benefits
- Competitive salary package commensurate with qualifications and experience.
- Full-time employment with an established construction company.
- Opportunities to work on a diverse range of residential and commercial construction projects.
- A collaborative working environment with experienced construction professionals.
- Opportunities for ongoing professional development and career progression.
About us
Duffy Kennedy Constructions is an established Sydney-based construction company delivering a diverse range of residential, commercial and other building projects. With extensive experience in the construction industry, we are committed to delivering high-quality projects through effective project management, technical expertise and close collaboration between our office and on-site teams. As our construction activities continue to develop, we are strengthening our internal technical capabilities to support efficient project delivery and maintain high standards across our operations.

candidates.content_text:
Kickstart Your Career in Engineering Drafting! 
Ready to turn your interest in design and engineering into a career? 
Whether you’re finishing Year 12, recently left school or studying Drafting at TAFE, this is your opportunity to get started in the engineering industry. 
STP Consultants is looking for an enthusiastic Junior Structural Draftsperson to join our growing Brisbane team. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers and drafters, gain hands-on experience and learn how the drawings you create become part of real projects across Queensland. 
You don’t need years of experience. We’re looking for someone with the right attitude, curiosity and willingness to learn. 
Why you’ll love working here 
Start building your career   Get hands-on experience from day one and develop practical Structural drafting skills while learning from experienced engineers and drafters. 
Work on real projects   Go beyond the classroom and see how structural engineering projects come together. You’ll contribute to drawings and documentation used throughout projects from concept and design through to delivery. 
Learn from experienced people   Ask questions, share ideas and learn from people who genuinely want to help you develop. You’ll receive guidance and mentoring as your skills and confidence grow. 
Be part of a great team   Join a close-knit, collaborative team where people support each other, work together and enjoy what they do. 
Work in Fortitude Valley   Our Brisbane office is in the heart of Fortitude Valley, close to public transport, cafés, restaurants and everything the city has to offer.
The Opportunity  
As you develop your skills, you’ll have the opportunity to: 
- Assist with preparing structural drawings, plans and project documentation. 
- Work with engineers and experienced drafters to produce clear, accurate and high-quality drawings. 
- Learn industry standards, guidelines and best-practice drafting processes. 
- Develop your understanding of how structural engineering projects are designed and delivered. 
- Participate in project discussions and meetings to build your understanding of project requirements. 
- Carry out basic drawing and documentation checks with guidance from experienced team members. 
- Take on more responsibility as your skills and confidence develop. 
About you: 
You could be a great fit if you are: 
- A Year 12 student, recent school leaver, or currently studying Residential Drafting, or an equivalent qualification at TAFE.
- Genuinely interested in structural drafting, design and engineering. 
- Curious and keen to learn new skills. 
- Detail-oriented and take pride in producing accurate work. 
- A good communicator who is comfortable asking questions and taking feedback. 
- Reliable, organised and willing to have a go at new challenges. 
- Someone who enjoys working with others and being part of a team. 
- An Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident. 
Most importantly, bring your enthusiasm and willingness to learn. We’ll help you turn it into a career. 
What’s in it for you? 
- 
Career development: Build your skills through hands-on experience, mentoring and ongoing professional development. 
- 
Flexibility: Enjoy a 9-day fortnight, flexible working hours and the option to purchase additional leave. 
- 
Competitive remuneration: A package that reflects your experience and contribution. 
- 
Recognition and rewards: Employee referral rewards and recognition programs. 
- 
Great culture: Work with supportive people in a friendly, collaborative environment, with regular team and social events. 
- 
Wellbeing support: Access to a confidential Employee Assistance Program. 
- 
Long-term opportunity: Build your career with an established, Australian-owned engineering consultancy. 
About STP Consultants  
For more than 20 years, STP Consultants has been helping shape communities across Queensland. 
We’re a privately owned, multidisciplinary engineering consultancy, bringing together expertise across Civil, Structural, Mechanical, Electrical, Hydraulic, Fire and Seismic engineering. Our teams work on a diverse range of projects across Queensland, giving you the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals and see the many different paths an engineering career can take. 
Our values of Potential, Respect, Integrity, Deliver and Engage shape the way we work with our clients and with each other. 
We’re proud of our approachable leaders, supportive team environment and commitment to developing people and delivering quality engineering outcomes. 
Ready to get started?   
If you’re looking for more than just a first job and want to build a career in engineering, we’d love to hear from you. 
Click Apply and send us your Resume and Cover Letter. 
In your cover letter, tell us: 
1. Why you’re interested in starting a career in structural drafting.   
2. What interests you about joining STP Consultants. 
STP Consultants is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and welcome applications from all backgrounds.

- Experience in using Revit and AutoCAD to produce architectural and civil documents
- High degree of accuracy and attention to detail with excellent planning and organisation skills
- Well-developed understanding and appreciation of architecture and landscape architecture, and how these design disciplines impact technical civil engineering design considerations
- Experience working in a diverse range of projects big and small for all types of clients from small extensions to townhouse/apartment developments to schools, pavilions, and clubhouses
- Experience working autonomously
- Appropriate time management skills and flexibility to allow for the management of a varying workload
- Fantastic interpersonal skills
About us
NOTAZ International is a growing Australian engineering consultancy with over 25 years of experience in the steel, mining, mineral processing, energy, and infrastructure sectors. Since 1999, we have delivered engineering excellence across more than 180 industrial projects, working alongside leading global technology providers and supporting clients from concept through to project execution. We value technical excellence, collaboration, and practical thinking.

The City of Canada Bay is a thriving, colourful community, surrounded by the beautiful bays of Sydney Harbour. The area is also known for its parklands, cycle paths and walkways. City of Canada Bay Council’s values underpin how we operate: 
We act with integrity| We empower our people| We are respectful| We work together| We innovate.

We are seeking an enthusiastic and capable Infrastructure Engineer to join our team and contribute to the planning, design and delivery of infrastructure projects that support our growing community.
This is an opportunity to apply your engineering expertise across a diverse range of infrastructure projects, from initial investigations and design through to construction, project delivery and contract management.
About the Role
You will assist with the development and delivery of infrastructure engineering projects, preparing designs, project plans, cost estimates, engineering specifications and tender documentation.
You will work across both operational and capital works, undertaking site investigations, inspections and project reviews, while providing practical engineering advice and recommendations to support quality project outcomes.
Key Responsibilities:
 - Assist with the planning, design and delivery of infrastructure projects.
 - Conduct site investigations and inspections and provide recommendations to address infrastructure issues.
 - Prepare project plans, engineering designs, specifications, cost estimates and tender documentation.
 - Monitor project works to ensure compliance with approved scope, specifications and objectives.
 - Support contract management and project administration.
 - Prepare reports, correspondence, grant submissions and other project documentation.
 - Assist with environmental assessments and obtaining relevant project approvals.
 - Provide professional and responsive service to internal stakeholders, contractors and the community.
 - Identify opportunities to improve project delivery, operational efficiency and service outcomes.
 - Promote Council’s work health and safety, risk management and environmental responsibilities.
 - Provide informed engineering recommendations based on project investigations and technical information.
About you
To be successful in this position, you will ideally have the following:
 - Currently undertaking, or recently completed, a tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering, or Project Management
 - Demonstrated project and time management skills, with the ability to prioritise tasks and meet deadlines.
 - Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel and Outlook, as well as relevant project management, database and design/drafting software such as AutoCAD.
 - A current Class C Driver Licence.
What’s on offer
We are offering a remuneration between $79,533 to $91,463 per annum plus Super.
The City of Canada Bay also offers excellent employee benefits which include:
 - A range of flexible work arrangements including hybrid work from home arrangements
 - A supportive, energetic, and passionate team
 - Significant leave benefits (sick/personal leave, health and wellbeing leave, access to Long Service leave after 5 years)
 - Continuous training, support, and leadership development
 - Health and Wellbeing programs (Yoga classes, Fitness Passport, Flu vaccinations, Skin Cancer Checks)
 - And much, much more!
Want to know more?
Further information regarding the requirements of this role can be found in the attached Position Description, alternatively for a confidential discussion please contact Vincenzo Camuglia, Coordinator, Infrastructure Design on 02 9911 6287 or email Vincenzo.Camuglia@canadabay.nsw.gov.au 
How to apply
Candidates MUST apply online. Applications close 11:30pm, Thursday 22 October 2026 and will not be accepted through any other medium.
If you have any accessibility requirements, please feel free to contact Grace Aberin on 02 9121 0238  or email  grace.aberin@canadabay.nsw.gov.au   to discuss.
The City of Canada Bay Council is a Child Safe Organisation that recognises and advocates for the rights of Children and Young People and are committed to a Safe Workplace.
The City of Canada Bay Council is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer committed to maintaining, growing and supporting a diverse, respectful, collaborative & inclusive workplace. We welcome and encourage applications from diverse community groups and ages including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, LGBTIQA+, people with disabilities, and other diversity groups.

candidates.content_text:
GRADUATE / JUNIOR ESTIMATOR – COMMERCIAL CONSTRUCTION
Cairns, QLD | Full-Time | Graduate / Entry Level
WIP Construction is looking for a motivated Graduate or Junior Estimator to join our Cairns-based team. This is an office-based position located in Cairns, Queensland. Applicants must be based in Cairns or willing to relocate.
This is an opportunity for someone who wants to build a career in commercial construction estimating. You don't need previous experience as an Estimator, we're more interested in finding someone with the right aptitude, attitude and genuine desire to learn.
You may be a recent graduate, currently studying, or at the beginning of your construction career and looking for an opportunity to develop practical, hands-on experience within an established commercial construction company.
The Role
Working alongside our experienced estimating and project team, you'll learn how commercial construction projects are priced, tendered and ultimately delivered.
As your experience develops, you'll be involved in:
- Reviewing construction drawings, specifications and tender documentation
- Assisting with quantity take-offs and pricing
- Preparing and issuing subcontractor and supplier enquiries
- Reviewing and comparing quotations
- Assisting with tender submissions
- Understanding project scope, methodology and construction requirements
- Building relationships with subcontractors and suppliers
- Working with our project delivery team to understand how estimates translate into live projects
- Developing your knowledge of commercial construction costs, trades and procurement
We don't expect you to know how to do all of this on day one. We'll teach you.
What we do expect is that you genuinely want to learn.
We're looking for someone who is curious, switched-on and interested in understanding how and why things are built and what they cost.
You may be studying or have recently completed a qualification in:
- Construction Management
- Quantity Surveying
- Civil Engineering
- Building & Construction
- Project Management
- Engineering
- Or another relevant construction-related discipline
We're also open to applicants from other backgrounds who can demonstrate strong numerical, analytical and problem-solving skills and a genuine interest in pursuing a career in construction estimating.
Previous estimating experience is not required.
More important to us is someone who:
- Has strong numerical and analytical skills
- Has excellent attention to detail
- Can read information carefully and ask questions when something doesn't make sense
- Is organised and able to manage competing priorities
- Communicates confidently and professionally
- Takes ownership of their work
- Has a genuine interest in building a long-term career in commercial construction
WIP Construction is an established Cairns-based commercial construction company delivering projects throughout Cairns and Far North Queensland.
You'll be joining a team where you'll have the opportunity to learn from experienced construction professionals and gain exposure to real commercial projects from tender through to delivery.
This isn't a graduate role where you'll spend months watching from the sidelines.
You'll be given real work, real responsibility and plenty of support while you develop your skills.
For the right person, there is significant opportunity to grow within the business and develop into an experienced Estimator.
If you're motivated, good with numbers, interested in construction and looking for somewhere to start your career, we'd like to hear from you.
Apply through SEEK with your resume and a short cover letter telling us a little about yourself, what you're currently studying or have completed, and why estimating and commercial construction interests you.

Life at Fulton Hogan is about making the most of opportunities, taking responsibility, and making it happen. We don't stand still - there are always opportunities to do more and do better.
