We offer great benefits, including corporate health and fitness programs, health insurance discounts, personal banking support, a range of retailer discounts, up to 18 weeks paid primary carers parental leave and up to 10 days paid secondary carers leave, access to our Employee Assistance Program (including your immediate family), and the option to take more time for yourself throughout the year with our Purchase Leave Policy.
- Want to help us better the communities we live and work in? Our purpose of creating, connecting, and caring for communities is more than a saying to us - it's a way of thinking, working, and living because we're locals too, and seek to give back in ways that strengthen and build resilient communities. We do this because we genuinely care, enjoy what we do, and even manage to have some fun along the way! You'll find us partnering with local and national community groups, like Clontarf Foundation and Black Dog Institute, in addition to indigenous groups and social enterprises, to ensure that our good work positively impacts and brings about sustainable change within our industry.
- Do we offer a 'competitive' salary package? Of course! Speak to our Talent Acquisition or People & Culture team to learn more.
What's on offer?
With the continued growth and diversification of our business, we are looking to appoint a Civil Estimator to join our Northern Region (QLD) Infrastructure business based in Eight Mile Plains.
Fulton Hogan is offering an exciting career path for a Civil Construction Professional to become an established estimator within the wider Fulton Hogan Infrastructure Services business. Key clients include National Defence, State Government, Local Government and the private sector throughout Queensland. 
You will be provided with direct support from the local business and formal mentoring from the National Civil Estimating Manager to develop and grow your estimating prowess and unlock your full potential. We will provide initial and ongoing training in the use of Expert Estimator Genesis.
You may be an existing Estimator, a Project Engineer or a Civil construction professional seeking a new career path without the rigorous demands of site-based roles. Substantial delivery phase and demonstrated site experience is essential to this role. You will have great communication skills with a good rapport with clients, subcontractors, and suppliers across the industry and enjoy working in a team environment. 
Reporting directly to the FHI Northern Sales & Tendering Manager you will be responsible for:
- Managing the tender process from start to finish including ensuring all elements of the tender are considered by the appropriate stakeholders and completed within the allotted time.
- Reviewing all tender documentation including specifications, quality, safety, and other requirements, as well as attending onsite tender briefings as required from time to time.
- Developing a winning construction methodology, including staging plans and verifying client schedules, programming the scope of works according to the construction methodology, assessing duration and productivity, and conducting win/loss reporting.
- Ensuring resource rates used are based on market rates & conditions, coordinating and sending out subcontractor/supply pricing packages, and performing overall quote analysis.
- Undertaking first principals estimates for various elements of civil construction, in conjunction with subcontractor pricing to ensure best for project outcomes
- Preparing detailed cost reports, summaries, and presentations for internal stakeholders and clients, providing presentations on project feasibility, budget adherence, innovations and cost-savings.
 To be successful we are seeking:
- Intermediate knowledge within the Civil Construction Industry.
- Demonstrated experience and technical knowledge of civil infrastructure projects, pricing from first principles and/or delivering projects on site with ambitions to transition into a full-time Civil Estimator role.
- Excellent communication and presentation skills including writing.
- Ability to construct detailed Construction Programs in MS Project or similar.
- Detailed knowledge of estimating software such as Expert Estimator or equivalent estimating packages will be highly regarded, but not essential.
 This position may require ad hoc travel.
Our people share the same set of values that keep us REAL. Respect, Energy and Effort, Attitude and Leadership encapsulate what we stand for at Fulton Hogan and encourage us to foster a diverse and inclusive culture where we listen to, care for, celebrate, and respect everyone.
We are committed to reconciliation and building and nurturing respectful relationships with First Nations peoples. Through our First Nations Engagement Strategy and Reconciliation Action Plan (RAP), we aim to promote opportunities, cultural understanding and partnerships that celebrate and acknowledge the contributions of Indigenous communities.
If our values resonate with you, please submit an application for the position. If you're not sure that you meet 100% of the selection criteria, that's okay, we would still like to hear from you and potentially discuss how your skills could be utilised at Fulton Hogan.
For over 90 years, Fulton Hogan has been delivering high-quality infrastructure to improve the lives of people every day. Our 10,000+ team works in every kind of weather and environment, creating, connecting, and caring for communities across Australia, New Zealand and the South Pacific.

Doolee is a leading civil construction company operating across Australia, with offices in WA and NSW, delivering complex, high-quality infrastructure projects across a diverse range of sectors. We are currently seeking a skilled and experienced Civil Engineer to join our dynamic team and contribute to the successful delivery of our projects.
Position Overview
As a Civil Engineer, you will be responsible for planning, designing, organising and overseeing civil engineering and construction projects from planning through to delivery. You will provide technical engineering expertise across project design, construction methodologies, materials, quality standards, cost management and site coordination, working closely with project managers, site personnel, subcontractors, consultants and clients to ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with engineering requirements, specifications and Australian Standards.
Key Responsibilities
- Plan, design, organise and oversee the construction and delivery of civil engineering and infrastructure projects.
- Review, interpret and prepare engineering drawings, plans, specifications, construction methods and procedures.
- Organise and coordinate site labour, construction materials, plant and equipment to support the efficient delivery of project works.
- Establish and maintain detailed programs for the coordination of site activities, resources and construction works.
- Undertake site inspections, investigations and assessments to determine project requirements, site conditions and construction feasibility.
- Study engineering drawings and specifications to assist with cost estimates, quantity measurements, cost plans and budgetary control.
- Monitor project costs, construction progress and resource requirements, identifying potential cost impacts and delays.
- Monitor changes to designs and assess their impact on project costs, construction methodology, program and resources.
- Measure, value and assist with the negotiation and management of variations to designs, scope and construction works.
- Coordinate with project managers, engineers, supervisors, subcontractors, consultants and clients to ensure effective project delivery.
- Assist with the design and development of civil infrastructure, including earthworks, roads, drainage, pavements and associated civil works.
- Ensure engineering and construction activities comply with relevant Australian Standards, legislation, safety requirements and project specifications.
- Identify project risks, construction issues and opportunities for improvement and implement appropriate engineering and corrective solutions.
- Provide technical support throughout the project lifecycle, from planning and design through to construction and completion.
Qualifications and Experience
- Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or a relevant engineering discipline.
- Demonstrated experience in civil construction and infrastructure projects.
- Experience in planning, coordinating and overseeing civil engineering and construction works.
- Demonstrated ability to interpret and work from engineering drawings, plans, specifications and construction documentation.
- Experience with project cost estimation, quantity measurement, cost control and budget management.
- Experience assessing design changes and managing variations to project scope, cost and construction methodology.
- Strong knowledge of relevant Australian Standards, construction legislation, quality requirements and workplace health and safety obligations.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and relevant engineering/design software.
- White Card and relevant construction qualifications or tickets will be highly regarded.
- Previous experience in a Project Engineer, Site Engineer or Graduate Civil Engineer role will be highly regarded.
Benefits:
- A competitive remuneration package aligned with experience.
- Clear pathways for professional development and internal progression.
- FIFO 2/1 roster, providing work-life balance.
- Employee assistance program.
Doolee is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Further your career with an organisation that is invested in your success.

At Maker Consulting Services, you'll join a growing Newcastle team delivering civil engineering projects across NSW. From residential subdivisions and industrial developments to roads, stormwater infrastructure and public domain works, you'll be involved throughout the project lifecycle alongside experienced professionals who value collaboration, practical thinking and quality outcomes. 
Whether you're a Mid-Level Engineer ready to take the next step or a Senior Engineer seeking greater autonomy, project influence and mentoring opportunities, this role provides the platform to build the career you want. As our Newcastle office grows, so will your opportunity to lead projects, strengthen client relationships and help shape the future of the team. 
Build a Career That Works for You 
The best engineering careers are about more than interesting projects. They're built on continuous learning, strong professional relationships and the opportunity to develop without compromising the things that matter outside of work.  
That's the environment we've built at Maker - one where talented engineers are trusted to make decisions, supported to keep learning, and where knowledge is shared, ideas are encouraged and achievements are recognised. We're proud of the collaborative team we've built, and the projects you work on won't just be drawings on a screen - they'll become the roads, neighbourhoods and public spaces that shape communities across NSW. 
Along the way, you'll enjoy:

- Ownership of meaningful projects from concept through to construction.  
- An employee-owned business where your contribution matters.  
- Career progression based on capability and contribution, not simply years of experience.  
- Mentoring, technical development and support towards CPEng.  
- A diverse range of projects that continue to broaden your experience.  
- Flexible working arrangements and a collaborative team that celebrates success.

You'll play an important role in delivering projects that leave a lasting impact on the communities they're built for. 
Working alongside experienced engineers, designers and project managers, you'll be involved from early concept design and approvals through to detailed design and construction support. You'll work directly with clients, councils, service authorities, contractors and multidisciplinary teams to deliver practical solutions that balance technical quality with commercial outcomes. 
Depending on your experience, you'll take ownership of projects or key design packages while continuing to develop your technical, client management and leadership capability. As you grow, you'll also have opportunities to mentor engineers, contribute to business development and influence the direction of our Newcastle team. 
Your day-to-day work will include: 
- Delivering civil engineering design and documentation across land development and public infrastructure projects.  
- Designing roads, earthworks, stormwater drainage and associated civil infrastructure.  
- Coordinating with clients, councils, service authorities, contractors and project teams.  
- Managing deliverables from planning and approvals through to construction.  
- Developing practical and innovative engineering solutions.  
- Providing guidance and mentoring to graduate and junior engineers. 
About You 
You enjoy solving problems, take pride in producing quality work and value collaboration. With a naturally curious mindset, you’re motivated to learn, communicate well and enjoy taking ownership of your work. Most importantly, you're looking for a place where you can continue developing as an engineer, project leader and mentor. 
You will also bring: 
- A Bachelor of Civil Engineering.  
- 3-8+ years' consulting experience, ideally in land development or civil infrastructure.
- Experience designing roads, earthworks, stormwater drainage and associated infrastructure.  
- Experience using 12d, together with AutoCAD/Civil 3D, DRAINS and MUSIC.  
- A sound understanding of Australian Standards, local government requirements and engineering design principles.  
- Strong communication, report writing and stakeholder management skills.  
- CPEng accreditation, or the ambition to achieve it with support from the business. 
Ready for What's Next? 
If this sounds like the opportunity you've been looking for, we'd love to hear from you. Please submit your resume and a cover letter outlining your experience, what attracted you to Maker and what you're looking for in the next stage of your career. 
We're not just looking for someone to fill a position. We're looking for someone who wants to build a career with us and help shape the future of our Newcastle team.

candidates.content_text:
Site / Project Engineer - Civil & Concrete
Oakleigh Civil - South Australia
Join a growing South Australian civil construction company and build your career across project engineering, construction delivery, estimating and commercial management. 
About Oakleigh Civil 
Oakleigh Civil is a South Australian civil construction company specialising in civil infrastructure and structural concrete projects. Our capabilities include formwork, reinforcement, concrete placement and excavation. 
We work with on major infrastructure projects across metropolitan and regional South Australia, as well as interstate. 
Our work spans water infrastructure, defence, renewable energy, roads, mining and electrical infrastructure. 
Our experienced team takes a practical approach to delivering projects safely and to a very high standard. We value strong client relationships and take pride in being a contractor our clients can rely on.
About the role 
We are seeking a motivated Site / Project Engineer with at least three years’ construction experience to join our growing team. 
Working closely with the Construction Manager, company management, site supervisors and clients, you will help plan, coordinate and deliver projects from tender stage through to completion.  
The role combines site-based project management, estimating and commercial responsibilities. Unlike a traditional site engineering role, you will have exposure to the full project lifecycle, including estimating, procurement, construction delivery, cost control, variations, progress claims and project close-out. 
The successful candidate will be expected to take ownership of assigned projects, identify issues early and work with the project team to develop practical solutions. 
This position suits someone who is looking to broaden their capabilities, take greater responsibility and develop their career within a growing civil construction business.
Key responsibilities 
- Plan and coordinate construction activities with site supervisors to meet project requirements and construction programs. 
- Take ownership of allocated projects from planning through to completion. 
- Maintain regular communication with clients regarding project progress, upcoming works and any issues requiring resolution. 
- Review drawings, specifications and scope documents, identify issues, discrepancies, risks and constructability issues. 
- Assist with estimating, quantity take-offs, quotations and tender submissions. 
- Prepare and maintain project schedules, budgets, forecasts and progress reports. 
- Monitor project costs, cost-to-complete and forecasts. 
- Prepare and track project costs, variations and progress claims. 
- Coordinate procurement of materials, subcontractors and suppliers in accordance with project requirements and programs. 
- Coordinate project quality requirements, including ITP’s, inspections, testing, NCR’s and handover documentation. 
- Maintain accurate project documentation, registers, correspondence and records. 
- Support site safety requirements and work with supervisors to ensure works are planned and delivered safely. 
- Provide practical engineering and constructability advice to site teams. 
- Build and maintain effective relationships with clients, contractors and suppliers. 
About you 
- A degree in Civil Engineering or a relevant engineering discipline. 
- At least three years’ experience as a Site or Project Engineer in construction. 
- Experience in civil infrastructure or structural concrete works; formwork, reinforcement and concrete placement experience will be highly regarded. 
- Ability to interpret construction drawings, specifications and technical requirements. 
- Understanding of construction programming, project cost control, quality assurance and WHS requirements. 
- Strong organisation, communication and problem-solving skills. 
- Experience with variations, progress claims and project documentation. 
- Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple projects. 
- A practical approach, initiative and willingness to work closely with site supervisors and site crews. 
- Ability to identify problems early and take ownership of finding practical solutions. 
- Willingness and ability to work away from home when required. 
- A genuine desire to develop your skills and progress your career within a growing construction business. 
Why Join Oakleigh Civil?
- Varied projects: Work on civil infrastructure and structural concrete projects in metropolitan and regional South Australia, as well as interstate. 
- Broader experience: Gain exposure to the full project lifecycle, including estimating, procurement, construction, commercial management and project close out. 
- Direct involvement: Work closely with Construction Manager, company management and experienced site teams with the opportunity to influence how projects are delivered. 
- Career development: Build your capabilities across project management, estimating and commercial management, with genuine pathway to increase responsibility as the company grows. 
- Make a Contribution: Bring your ideas and help improve the way we work that supports Oakleigh Civil’s continued growth. 
Apply now 
If you’re looking to take the next step in your engineering career with Oakleigh Civil, apply through SEEK with your CV and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience.

About the role
As a Subdivision Engineer you will play a vital role in maintaining Glen Eira’s public infrastructure. You will assess applications, certify plans, and ensure that all public assets are built to the highest standards. You will also help manage development bonds and agreements, inspect construction works, and provide engineering advice throughout the development lifecycle.
You will also support the community by responding to enquiries, investigating complaints, and providing clear, technical advice to residents, developers, and internal teams.
Other responsibilities include:
- Liaising with utility providers to coordinate works within Council Road reserves
- Reviewing and approving stormwater drainage and water quality assessments.
- Assessing subdivision applications and certifying plans in accordance with the Subdivision Act 1988 and Planning and Environment Act 1987.
- Reviewing and approving utility consent applications under the Road Management Act 2004.
- Assist with reviewing town planning applications and engineering assessments to ensure compliance with permits, Council standards, and policies.
About you
Our ideal candidate will have a bachelor's degree in civil engineering and be eligible for Membership of the Institute of Engineers.  You will have a solid understanding of the Subdivision Act 1988, Planning and Environment Act 1987, and Road Management Act 2004. You should be confident using GIS systems, Microsoft Windows, and customer service platforms like Pathway.
Strong communication skills are essential, as this role often needs to translate complex technical concepts into clear, practical advice for a diverse range of stakeholders.
The following is also required:
- Minimum 2 years’ experience in local government or statutory authority.
- Bachelor's degree in civil engineering (or equivalent).
- Eligible for Membership of the Institute of Engineers.
- Strong knowledge of relevant legislation including the Subdivision Act, Planning and Environment Act, and Road Management Act.
- Excellent communication and customer service skills.
- A Victorian Driver’s License is essential.
Not meeting all the requirements for this role? We value diverse experiences for positive community outcomes. If you're excited about the position but don't perfectly align with the criteria, we still encourage you to apply.

- Reward and recognition programs
- Comprehensive leave entitlements

The City of Glen Eira is a dynamic municipality located within the southeast metropolitan region of Melbourne, approximately 10 kilometres from the CBD. Council provides a range of services to over 155,000 residents from more than 160 cultural backgrounds and over 16,000 businesses.
Glen Eira City Council is a collaborative, values-based organisation that strives for innovation. Our 1,370 employees bring their diverse backgrounds and varied experiences and perspectives to an inclusive and flexible work environment, creating a unique and vibrant culture that is representative of the municipality it services.

- Assist with preparing project estimates, including material quantities, labour and costs

- Assist with material takeoffs for steel framing and other construction materials
- Review project drawings, specifications and other documents to identify project requirements

- Good understanding of mathematics and attention to detail
- Ability to read and understand architectural and engineering drawings

- Good written and verbal communication skills
- Organised and able to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines

bullets: High-Rise Towers & Landmark Developments
Global Engineering Consultancy - Australian owned
Work on some of Sydney's most exciting large-scale projects
candidates.content_text:
Are you a talented Structural Revit Drafter, BIM Technician or Revit Modeller looking for the opportunity to work on genuinely exciting, large-scale projects?
 We are working with a highly respected, Australian-owned engineering consultancy with an impressive global footprint and offices around the world. Their growing Sydney office is looking to welcome an experienced Structural Revit Drafter/BIM Technician to join the team.
 This is a fantastic opportunity to get involved in some seriously impressive projects! Think high-rise towers, iconic commercial developments, major mixed-use precincts and landmark buildings.
 The Sydney team is made up of some of the most talented structural engineers in the state, and with an incredibly strong pipeline of major projects already secured, you'll have the opportunity to get stuck into exciting work from day one.
 The Role
 You'll be joining a relatively small but growing structural drafting team in Sydney, which presents a brilliant opportunity for someone looking to make their mark and grow their career.
 You'll also be working with an awesome manager who is genuinely passionate about developing people. Someone who will mentor, guide, encourage and support you whenever needed, while giving you the autonomy and trust to do what you do best.
 As the Sydney office continues to grow, so will the opportunities for you to develop your skills, take on more responsibility and progress your career.
 Key Responsibilities
 - Develop and produce high-quality structural Revit models and detailed documentation for major building projects.
 - Work on large-scale developments including high-rise towers, commercial buildings and mixed-use precincts.
 - Collaborate closely with structural engineers, architects and other disciplines throughout the design and documentation process.
 - Produce detailed structural drawings covering reinforced concrete, structural steel and other building elements.
 - Coordinate BIM models and identify and resolve clashes and design coordination issues.
 - Contribute to the delivery of projects from concept design through to construction documentation.
 - Maintain high standards of modelling accuracy, quality and BIM compliance.
 - Work collaboratively with the wider engineering and drafting teams to deliver technically challenging projects.
 What We're Looking For
 - Experience as a Structural Revit Drafter, BIM Technician or Revit Modeller within a structural engineering consultancy.
 - Strong Revit modelling and structural documentation skills.
 - Experience working on building structures, ideally multi-storey, commercial or large-scale developments.
 - Good understanding of reinforced concrete and structural steel detailing.
 - Familiarity with BIM processes, coordination and model management.
 - Strong attention to detail and the ability to work collaboratively with engineers and other disciplines.
 - A positive attitude, willingness to learn and genuine enthusiasm for working on technically challenging projects.
 Experience working on large projects would be fantastic, but we're equally interested in speaking with talented structural drafters who are ready to take that next step and gain exposure to larger, more complex developments.
Why You'll Love This Opportunity
 - Large projects - Work on high-rise towers, landmark buildings and major developments.
 - Outstanding project pipeline - A strong pipeline of secured, large-scale projects ready for you to get involved in.
 - Work with the best - Collaborate with some of Sydney's most talented and experienced structural engineers.
 - Fantastic manager and mentor - Join a team led by someone who genuinely cares about your development, provides guidance and encourages you to succeed.
 - Small, growing drafting team - An exciting opportunity to make a real impact and grow alongside the Sydney business.
 - Genuine career progression - As the team expands, there will be opportunities to take on greater responsibility and develop your career.
 If you've been waiting for an opportunity to work on genuinely exciting projects, learn from some of the best engineers in the industry and be part of a growing team where your career can really take off, this could be exactly what you're looking for!
 Apply today or contact Natasha at Cookson & Roberts on 0410 777 473 for a confidential chat.
 All enquiries will be treated in the strictest confidence.

candidates.title: Draftsperson
candidates.abstract: Intermediate Drafter designing innovative structures for events nationally and globally.
screening_questions: Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
What's your expected annual base salary?
How many years' experience do you have as a draftsperson?
How much notice are you required to give your current employer?
candidates.content_text:
About the role
The Drafter role is an intermediate level position, reporting to the National Drafting Manager and management staff in the Melbourne office. As part of the Drafting and Design Team based at the Sydney facility in Warwick Farm, you will be designing and drawing innovative structures for events held nationally and globally. Training and on-going guidance are provided.
Key responsibilities
- Preparing drawings and technical plans that comply with customer specifications, BCA standards, and business drafting guidelines
- Liaising with the production, operations, and fabrication teams to ensure structures are practical to build and make the most of equipment in stock
- Occasionally interfacing with customers to clarify their requirements
- Attending site periodically to gain a feel for the event and structures being designed
- Visiting the warehouse to familiarise yourself with the equipment being drawn
- Document preparation and document management
- Assisting with general business and office activities, as directed
About you
- Experience in AutoCAD for 2D and 3D modelling
- A flair for calculations and problem solving, with a passion for designing innovative practical structures
- Sound time management skills and the ability to work accurately while adhering to strict deadlines
- Exceptional communication skills - listening, written and verbal
- Ability to learn quickly and to work autonomously and as part of a team
- A 'can do' attitude, good attention to detail and pride in your work
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, Word) and Google Chrome, with knowledge of Dropbox and Adobe Acrobat
- Australian Citizenship or Permanent Residency, with a valid working visa and Tax File Number
About us
Clifton Productions is a leading supplier in the Event industry supplying concert staging, temporary seating and temporary structures for events in the Australian and International market. Head office is in Melbourne, with fully staffed offices and warehouses in Melbourne, Sydney and Brisbane. Our national drafting division is a small dedicated team based at our Sydney facility in Warwick Farm.
